brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the effect of a multi-component digital nudge intervention based on the Health Belief Model on breast cancer awareness, health beliefs, and screening behaviors among women aged 40-69. The study is a randomized controlled trial. The sample will consist of 64 women aged 40-69. The study will be conducted between November 2026 and July 2027 at the Şükrüpaşa Family Health Center in Erzurum, Turkey. Data will be collected using an Informed Consent Form, the Breast Cancer Awareness Scale, the Health Belief Model Scale for Mammography, and a screening behavior assessment form.
primary_outcomes: Mammography Screening Behavior
title: Effect of a Health Belief Model Based Digital Nudge Intervention on Breast Cancer Screening

brief_summary: This study is a prospective, single-center, single-arm early feasibility study, to establish safety and tolerability of FUS neuromodulation in patients with Binge Eating Disorder (BED)
primary_outcomes: Occurrence of Treatment Emergent Adverse Events
title: FUS Neuromodulation for Binge Eating Disorder

brief_summary: This study will examine how smartphone use recorded by the phone and daily sleep, sitting, and physical activity are related to neck posture, sensitivity to pressure, and body awareness in university students aged 18 to 30 years. One hundred students will complete seven days of smartphone and activity monitoring and clinical assessments. Among these students, 56 who have nonspecific neck pain for at least three months, average pain of at least 3 out of 10, and forward head posture will be randomly assigned to integrated myofascial release or a light-touch control. Both groups will receive six sessions over two weeks. An assessor who does not know the assigned group will measure outcomes before and after treatment and, where feasible, one month after treatment. The study will investigate whether myofascial release improves neck pain, pressure pain threshold, posture, movement, disability, and awareness.
primary_outcomes: Change in Pressure Pain Threshold
title: Digital Use, 24-Hour Movement Behaviors, and Myofascial Release in University Students With Neck Pain

Effectiveness will be assessed by measuring the reduction in intraocular pressure (IOP). Study results will support regulatory submissions to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and may also be used to support regulatory submissions and postmarketing surveillance activities in other countries.

brief_summary: This online randomized controlled trial will evaluate whether a short, wordless animated storytelling film increases positive attitudes and intentions toward seeking help for mental health concerns among U.S. adults aged 18 to 25. Participants will be recruited via Prolific and randomized in Stanford Qualtrics to view the film or to receive no intervention. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline, immediately after exposure, and at a brief follow-up one week later. All participants will be offered a downloadable list of free mental health resources; downloads will be recorded.
primary_outcomes: Mental Help-Seeking Attitudes Scale (MHSAS)
title: Short, Wordless Animated Storytelling to Promote Mental Health Help-Seeking in Young Adults: A U.S. Online Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) will be considered a clinically important complication of diabetes mellitus that may impair sensory function and interfere with the performance of daily activities involving the hands and feet. Sensory deficits may affect tactile perception, object manipulation, foot-related functional tasks, and the ability to interact safely with the surrounding environment.

The purpose of this study will be to investigate the effects of adaptive gamified sensory training combined with conventional physical therapy on sensory function, sensory integration during balance, and hand functional performance in patients with diabetic peripheral neuropathy.
primary_outcomes: Neuropathy Impairment Scale (NIS) - Sensory Subset
title: Adaptive Gamified Sensory Training on Sensory Function and Limb-Specific Functional Performance in Patients With Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate how well JNJ-101556143 plus Best Supportive Care (BSC) improves overall survival (the length of time a participant remains alive) compared with placebo plus BSC in participants with metastatic androgen pathway modulation-resistant prostate cancer (mAPMR). mAPMR is an advanced form of prostate cancer that has spread to other parts of the body and no longer responds to hormone treatments designed to block male hormones (androgens).
primary_outcomes: Overall Survival (OS)
title: A Study of JNJ-101556143 With Best Supportive Care in Participants With Metastatic Prostate Cancer

brief_summary:
This single-center, open-label, prospective pilot study aims to evaluate the feasibility, safety, and preliminary diagnostic performance of a minimally invasive gastric string sampling device combined with a rapid antigen assay for the detection of Helicobacter pylori infection.

A total of 40 participants with documented \^13C-urea breath test (UBT) results will be enrolled, including 30 UBT-positive and 10 UBT-negative participants. All participants will undergo gastric mucus collection using a disposable string sampling device, followed by H. pylori rapid antigen testing.

The primary objective is to assess the diagnostic sensitivity and specificity of the investigational test using \^13C-UBT as the reference standard. The secondary objective is to explore the correlation between the semi-quantitative test-line (T-line) color intensity of the rapid antigen assay and the corresponding UBT delta-over-baseline (DOB) values.
interventions: HP String Test With Rapid Antigen Assay
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic Sensitivity and Specificity of the HP String Test With Rapid Antigen Assay
title: Pilot Study of a Gastric String Test Combined With a Rapid Antigen Assay for Helicobacter Pylori Detection

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to collect information on the safety and performance of the remedē System in patients with central sleep apnea who are undergoing the remedē System implant procedure. The main question\[s\] it aims to answer \[is/are\]:

What is the incidence of serious adverse events related to the remedē System implant procedure, device, or delivered therapy through 12 months post implant.

Participants will complete 2 home sleep apnea tests and be asked about adverse events. All other data collected will be from standard of care visits.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of serious adverse events (SAEs) related to the remedē System implant procedure, device, or delivered therapy through 12 months post implant
title: Registry of Central Sleep Apnea Patients Undergoing remedē System Implant

brief_summary: External apical root resorption is a possible side effect of fixed orthodontic treatment, particularly in the upper front teeth. This randomized clinical trial was conducted to compare the amount and timing of root resorption associated with three different methods of retracting the upper anterior teeth using miniscrew anchorage. Sixty adult patients with Class II Division 1 malocclusion who required extraction of the upper first premolars were randomly allocated to one of three groups: a bidimensional bracket group, a hybrid dual-section archwire group, or a conventional sliding mechanics group. In all groups, the six upper anterior teeth were retracted together with the support of orthodontic miniscrews. Panoramic radiographs were obtained before treatment, after completion of leveling and alignment, and after completion of en-masse retraction. Root and crown lengths were measured on these radiographs to estimate external apical root resorption during the leveling and alignment phase, during the retraction phase, and over the complete observation period. The study also compared the pattern of resorption among the upper canines, lateral incisors, and central incisors.
primary_outcomes: External Apical Root Resorption of the Maxillary Anterior Teeth
title: Root Shortening With Three Different Methods of Upper Anterior Teeth Retraction

brief_summary: This is a single-arm, open-label, phase 2 clinical trial using a stratified Simon minimax two-stage design. The study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of low-dose apatinib (250 mg daily) combined with physician-selected single-agent chemotherapy (TPC, capecitabine preferred) in patients with HER2-positive or HER2-low advanced/metastatic breast cancer who progressed after prior ADC therapy (T-DXd or SHR-A1811). Patients are stratified by HER2 status, HR status, lines of prior ADC therapy, and metastasis sites. Approximately 56 patients will be enrolled. The primary endpoint is objective response rate (ORR). Secondary endpoints include PFS1, PFS2, TTP, safety, and OS.
primary_outcomes: Objective Response Rate (ORR)
title: Low-Dose Apatinib Plus Chemotherapy in ADC-Pretreated HER2-Positive and HER2-Low Advanced Breast Cancer

brief_summary:
WALLAS is a small observational study of 30 adults with complex wounds in the abdominal wall after surgery. All participants will receive negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) because their treating team considers it appropriate. This treatment uses a sealed dressing connected to a suction device. The study will not decide which treatment participants receive or change their usual care.

The main aim is to find out how the stiffness of the large arteries changes during treatment. Researchers will also examine whether larger reductions in wound size and inflammation are linked to larger reductions in artery stiffness.

An upper-arm cuff device will estimate artery stiffness by measuring how quickly pressure waves travel along the aorta, the body's main artery. Measurements are planned before treatment starts, around day 5, and when the first course of NPWT ends. Blood pressure will be taken into account when interpreting the results.

During planned dressing changes, researchers will record wound depth and, when safe and technically possible, measure the wound cavity using sterile saline. Photographs will document the wound. Results from routine blood tests will provide information about inflammation; no extra blood samples are required for research.

Wound recovery and further treatment will be followed for about six months after NPWT starts. The study will also assess how practical and safe the measurement procedures are. Because there is no comparison group, it cannot determine whether NPWT itself causes any changes in artery stiffness.
primary_outcomes: Change in aortic pulse wave velocity (PWVao) from baseline to cessation of the index NPWT episode
title: Arterial Stiffness During Negative Pressure Wound Therapy for Abdominal Wall Wounds

brief_summary: This multicenter study aims to characterize the language profiles of patients with various neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease (AD), Primary Progressive Aphasia (PPA), behavioral variant Frontotemporal Dementia (bvFTD), Dementia with Lewy Bodies (DLB), and Parkinson's disease (PD), using artificial intelligence (AI) models. By analyzing speech and language data collected during remote neuropsychological assessments, the researchers intend to identify objective linguistic biomarkers suitable for early and differential diagnosis, overcoming the limitations of traditional, invasive, and costly diagnostic tools. The project will develop and validate an AI-driven pipeline to provide scalable and individualized linguistic profiles, ultimately supporting personalized treatment strategies and improving clinical workflow efficiency in the Italian population.
interventions: Speech and language Test to support clinical diagnosis
primary_outcomes: Performance of AI-based language analysis in distinguishing diagnostic groups
title: Automated Language Analysis in Neurodegenerative Diseases: Application of Artificial Intelligence Models

brief_summary: This single-center, single-arm, open-label study evaluates the efficacy and safety of ultrasound-guided radiofrequency ablation (RFA) in women with symptomatic focal adenomyosis who wish to preserve the uterus. RFA is performed transvaginally under general anesthesia using the Myoblate system. Participants are followed at 3, 6 and 12 months (optionally 24 months) with transvaginal ultrasound and validated questionnaires (VAS, PBAC, EQ-5D-5L). The primary outcomes are the changes in pain severity and menstrual blood loss at 6 and 12 months compared with baseline.
interventions: Myoblate Radiofrequency Ablation System (Mygen V-1000 generator)
primary_outcomes: Change in pain severity (VAS) from baseline
Change in menstrual blood loss (PBAC score) from baseline
title: Ultrasound-Guided Radiofrequency Ablation for Focal Adenomyosis

brief_summary: This study goal was to assess the evolution of spatio-temporal and kinematic gait parameters in toddlers with unilateral cerebral palsy (UCP) receiving standard rehabilitation during the first 18 months after gait acquisition and to compare their gait characteristics with those of typically developing (TD) children. The hypothesis is that the biomechanical parameters of newly acquired gait of children with UCP and their differences compared to TD toddlers with the same walking experience will change over time.

brief_summary: This study will investigate whether daily supplementation with 400 mg of magnesium from a triple magnesium complex containing magnesium glycinate, magnesium malate, and magnesium citrate can improve body composition in young adults. Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either the magnesium complex or a placebo once daily for 8 weeks. Body composition, including body weight, body mass index, body fat percentage, muscle mass, waist circumference, hip circumference, and waist-to-hip ratio, will be assessed before and after the intervention. The study will compare changes in these measures between the magnesium and placebo groups to determine whether daily magnesium supplementation has beneficial effects on body composition.
primary_outcomes: Muscle mass
Body composition
title: Effects of Daily Magnesium Complex Supplementation on Body Composition in University Students

brief_summary:
The optimal timing for transition from controlled to assisted mechanical ventilation in patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) remains uncertain. Excessive spontaneous respiratory effort may promote injurious transpulmonary pressure swings and heterogeneous regional ventilation, whereas unnecessary prolongation of controlled ventilation may increase sedation exposure and diaphragmatic dysfunction.

This prospective, single-center physiological interventional study will enroll mechanically ventilated adults with ARDS and a PaO₂/FiO₂ ratio \>100 and ≤200 mmHg, measured during PEEP=5 cmH2O, who are receiving controlled mechanical ventilation. Participants will undergo a protocolized 30-minute transition from controlled to assisted mechanical ventilation after reduction of sedation sufficient to allow spontaneous respiratory activity.

Respiratory effort and drive, airway and esophageal pressures, respiratory flow, respiratory mechanics, gas exchange, and regional ventilation measured by electrical impedance tomography will be assessed before and during the transition. Participants will subsequently be followed for 48 hours to determine whether assisted ventilation can be maintained without return to fully controlled mechanical ventilation.
interventions: Protocolized Transition From Controlled to Assisted Mechanical Ventilation
primary_outcomes: Difference in Respiratory Mechanics between succesfull and failed transition using a pneumotachograph
Difference in Respiratory Mechanics between succesfull and failed transition using a pneumotachograph
Difference in Respiratory Mechanics between succesfull and failed transition using a pneumotachograph
Difference in Respiratory Mechanics between succesfull and failed transition using a pneumotachograph
title: Early Switch in Moderate ARDS

brief_summary:
Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is the most common cancer of the mouth and is often preceded by oral leukoplakia (OL), a white patch of the oral lining that can turn into cancer. At present it is difficult to predict which leukoplakias will become malignant, and OSCC is frequently diagnosed at a late stage. Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are RNA molecules that do not produce proteins but regulate genes and cell-signalling pathways, and they are being studied as markers of cancer.

This prospective diagnostic and prognostic accuracy study examines whether two lncRNAs, FENDRR and CRNDE, and two proteins, DUSP1 and DMBT1, can distinguish OL and OSCC from normal oral tissue and from each other, and whether they predict the course of the disease. Their performance is compared with markers of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR and ERK signalling pathways (PI3K, AKT, mTOR, ERK2 and MMP9), which are commonly activated in oral cancer.

Tissue is obtained from patients undergoing surgical removal of OL, OSCC, and from healthy volunteers undergoing routine minor gingival surgery (control group). No additional procedure is performed for the purpose of the study. The diagnosis and grade of each lesion are confirmed by two oral pathologists who are unaware of the laboratory results. FENDRR, CRNDE, PI3K, AKT and mTOR are measured by real-time RT-PCR, and DUSP1, DMBT1, ERK2 and MMP9 by ELISA.

The primary outcome is the diagnostic accuracy (area under the ROC curve, sensitivity and specificity) of each marker for OL versus controls, OSCC versus controls and OSCC versus OL. Secondary outcomes are the association of marker expression with clinicopathological features (histological grade, clinical stage, degree of invasion, invasive front, lymph node and distant metastasis, and malignant transformation of OL) and with disease-free and overall survival during 24 months of follow-up.

The study hypothesis is that low FENDRR, DUSP1 and DMBT1 and high CRNDE expression accompany progression from normal mucosa to OL and OSCC and are associated with a poorer outcome, so that these markers could support early diagnosis and risk assessment of oral potentially malignant and malignant lesions.
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic potential of FENDRR, CRNDE, DUSP1 and DMBT1
title: FENDRR and CRNDE With DUSP1 and DMBT1 in Oral Leukoplakia and Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma

brief_summary: Periodontitis and inflammatory bowel disease have been associated by meta-epidemiologic evidence, although their mechanistic connection needs to be further explored. Oral-gut axis is implicated in the pathogenesis of several chronic inflammatory conditions, but to date no studies have evaluated the impact of periodontal treatment on gut ecology. Thus, the present observational prospective study is aimed at investigating the effect of conventional periodontal therapy on the gut microbiome and parameters of systemic inflammation of patients diagnosed with inflammatory bowel disease.
primary_outcomes: Changes in microbiome alpha diversity measured from stool samples at 3 months
title: Effects Of Periodontal Therapy In Patients With Inflammatory Bowel Disease

brief_summary:
This study measures circulating immune-signalling molecules before thyroid surgery to determine whether they differ between patients whose thyroid nodule proves to be a differentiated thyroid carcinoma and patients whose nodule proves to be benign.

Adults scheduled for elective thyroidectomy for a thyroid nodule or nodular goiter are enrolled consecutively before surgery, while the nature of the nodule is still unknown. One additional blood tube is obtained during the routine preoperative blood sampling that is performed for every patient on the day of hospital admission, one day before surgery. No separate venipuncture, no additional test, no additional visit and no change to diagnosis, treatment or follow-up is involved.

Serum interleukin-17A, measured before surgery, is the primary outcome measure. Additional Treg/Th17-related cytokines, the interleukin-17A to interleukin-10 ratio, and systemic inflammatory indices calculated from the same blood draw are secondary outcome measures. Participants are assigned to the differentiated thyroid cancer group or the benign nodular goiter group after surgery, on the basis of the final histopathology report.
primary_outcomes: Preoperative serum interleukin-17A concentration
title: Serum Treg/Th17-Related Cytokines and Systemic Inflammatory Indices in Differentiated Thyroid Cancer

brief_summary: Survivors of Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) admissions often experience adverse mental health consequences, either as a result of, or associated with, their intensive care stay. Evidence-based digital cognitive behavioral therapy (dCBT) tools exist for both children and parents to learn cognitive behavioral strategies. In this feasibility study, we aim to measure the adoption and acceptability of a dCBT tool among PICU survivors and their parents. We hypothesize that \>50% of subjects will meet completion criteria for these programs, and that we will observe a trend toward improved anxiety scores.
primary_outcomes: Screen for Child Anxiety and Related Disorders (SCARED)
title: Building Resilience Through Anxiety Virtual Education in PICU Survivors

brief_summary: This is a single-center, randomized, open-label controlled trial with blinded outcome assessment and data analysis. Fifty adults with overweight or obesity (body mass index \[BMI\] \>= 24 kg/m2) and a sedentary lifestyle will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to one of two groups: (1) a transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) group, in which participants self-administer taVNS at the cymba conchae of both ears on alternating days (20 Hz, dense-disperse mode, twice daily, 30 minutes per session, 5 days per week for 4 weeks) in addition to a standardized lifestyle program; or (2) a control group receiving the lifestyle program alone. The lifestyle program prescribes a daily energy intake of 1,000-1,500 kcal (55-60% carbohydrate, 25-30% fat, 20% protein) plus aerobic exercise of at least 30 minutes per session, 3 times per week. The primary outcome is the change in visceral fat index (VFI) from baseline to week 4. Secondary outcomes include changes in body weight, BMI and body fat percentage, as well as changes in thalamocortical functional connectivity, effective (directed) connectivity, and whole-brain functional network topological properties assessed by resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), and their associations with changes in obesity-related indicators. Assessments are performed at baseline (week 0) and after the 4-week intervention (week 4).
interventions: Standardized lifestyle program (calorie-restricted diet plus aerobic exercise)
lead_sponsor: Guangdong Provincial Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine
primary_outcomes: Change in visceral fat index (VFI)
title: Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation Combined With Lifestyle Intervention for Visceral Fat Reduction in Adults With Overweight or Obesity

brief_summary:
This study compared two surgical techniques for patients with nasal polyps affecting both sides of the nose and sinuses. Nasal polyps were soft swellings that caused symptoms such as nasal blockage, nasal discharge, and reduced sense of smell. The study assessed whether the amount of blood lost during surgery and the time required to complete surgery differed between microdebrider-assisted and conventional functional endoscopic sinus surgery.

The randomized controlled study was conducted in the Department of Ear, Nose and Throat at Lahore General Hospital, Lahore, over six months. It included 56 patients aged 18-70 years whose symptoms had persisted despite at least eight weeks of medical treatment. Patients were randomly assigned to two groups of 28 using sealed envelopes. Both groups underwent surgery under general anesthesia. In the microdebrider-assisted group, a powered instrument that cut and suctioned tissue simultaneously was used to remove the polyps. In the conventional group, standard surgical instruments, including forceps and curettes, were used.

Blood loss was measured in milliliters using the fluid collected through suction, after subtracting irrigation fluid, and the change in surgical sponge weights. Operative duration was recorded in minutes. These measurements were compared between the two groups. The study hypothesis was that microdebrider-assisted and conventional surgery differed in intraoperative blood loss and operative duration.
primary_outcomes: Mean Intraoperative Blood Loss
Mean Operative Duration
title: Comparison of Intraoperative Outcomes of Microdebrider-Assisted Versus Conventional Functional Endoscopic Sinus Surgery in Patients With Sinonasal Polyposis

brief_summary: This is a first-in-human study of NI112, an investigational medicine given as an injection under the skin, in adults with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). The purpose of the study is to find out how safe NI112 is, how well it is tolerated, and how the body handles it after a single dose. Up to 40 adults with ALS will take part at up to three study centers in the United States. Participants will be assigned by chance to receive either a single dose of NI112 or a single dose of placebo (sterile salt water). The study tests up to seven dose levels, one after another, beginning with the lowest dose. A Safety Review Board reviews the safety information from each group of participants before the next, higher dose is given to a new group. Each participant stays in the hospital for 24 hours after the injection for safety monitoring and blood sampling, and returns for follow-up visits on Day 8 and Day 28. The study also measures the amount of NI112 in blood and in spinal fluid.

brief_summary:
We are conducting this clinical trial to find out whether Guominkang-a traditional Chinese herbal formula-is safe and effective for people with diabetic kidney disease (DKD).

DKD is a common complication of diabetes, affecting 20% to 40% of patients. If not well controlled, it can lead to chronic kidney disease or even kidney failure. Current treatments mainly focus on controlling blood sugar and blood pressure, but few therapies directly target immune inflammation, which plays a key role in DKD progression.

In earlier animal studies, Guominkang reduced urine protein and blood sugar in mice with DKD and appeared to work by balancing both metabolism and immune-inflammatory responses.

This pilot study will enroll 18 adults aged 18-70 years with mild-to-moderate kidney damage (CKD stages G1-G3) due to DKD. Participants will be divided into three groups (6 per group):

Observation group: receives standard care only (medications to control blood sugar, blood pressure, and lipids); Standard-dose group: standard care + 1 dose of Guominkang per day; Double-dose group: standard care + 2 doses of Guominkang per day. The treatment lasts 12 weeks, followed by a 4-week follow-up after stopping the study drug.

During the study, you will need to:

Take your assigned medication (or continue standard treatment) as directed; Visit the clinic at weeks 2, 4, 8, 12, and 4 weeks after stopping treatment; Provide blood and urine samples for testing (e.g., urine protein, blood sugar, cholesterol, kidney function).

We hope to answer two main questions:

Can Guominkang reduce urine protein in patients with DKD? Is Guominkang safe-what side effects might occur?
interventions: Standard Antihypertensive, Antidiabetic, and Lipid-Lowering Regimen
primary_outcomes: Change in Urine Albumin-to-Creatinine Ratio (UACR)
title: A Study on the Safety and Clinical Efficacy of Guominkang in the Treatment of Diabetic Kidney Disease

brief_summary:
Anxiety, depression and poor sleep are common in the last months of pregnancy and often occur together. Medication options during pregnancy are limited, so simple, safe non-drug methods are needed. Mandala coloring is an art therapy technique in which a person colors circular patterns; it helps focus attention on the present moment and may have a calming effect.

This randomized controlled trial will examine whether mandala coloring during the third trimester reduces depression, anxiety and stress, improves sleep, and reduces fear of childbirth. It will also look at birth outcomes and the childbirth experience. Pregnant women at 28 weeks of gestation who attend the obstetrics outpatient clinics of Malatya Training and Research Hospital will be randomly assigned to a mandala coloring group or a control group. Women in the mandala group will color two mandalas a week at home for 8 weeks (16 mandalas in total, about 20-30 minutes per session). Women in the control group will receive routine antenatal care only and will be offered the mandala materials after the study ends.
primary_outcomes: Change in Depression Score (DASS-21 Depression Subscale)
title: Mandala Coloring in Late Pregnancy

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate and compare the safety and efficacy of topical insulin and topical irradiated amniotic fluid gel in promoting wound healing in patients with epidermolysis bullosa (EB). Thirty patients with confirmed EB and suitable non-infected wounds were recruited from the Dermatology and Venereology Department, Tanta University Hospitals, Egypt. Wounds were assessed before and after treatment using wound surface area measurements, pain scores, clinical evaluation, and photographic documentation. Treatment was administered weekly for four consecutive weeks, with subsequent follow-up assessments. An untreated wound group served as the control. The study also evaluated patient satisfaction and treatment-related adverse effects.
primary_outcomes: Change in wound surface area
title: Topical Insulin Versus Irradiated Amniotic Fluid Gel for Wound Healing in Epidermolysis Bullosa

brief_summary: This observational registry collects retrospective and prospective, data from children and adults who use CE-marked MED-EL implantable (PMEI, BCI, or AMEI) or non-implantable (BCD) hearing solutions as part of routine care. Participants will be followed long term, potentially up to the lifetime of their hearing solution, to assess quality of life, hearing and speech performance, and device use. Data will be collected using routinely administered clinical tests and questionnaires to evaluate real-world outcomes across diverse populations and MED-EL hearing systems.

brief_summary: This prospective, single-arm, exploratory clinical study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of short-course radiotherapy (SCRT) sequentially followed by adebrelimab combined with chemotherapy as an organ-preservation strategy in patients with locally advanced resectable rectal cancer. Approximately 155 eligible patients will be enrolled after providing full written informed consent and passing screening, and will receive SCRT followed by adebrelimab plus chemotherapy. The primary efficacy endpoint is the complete response (CR) rate assessed at the end of Cycle 4 or Cycle 8 of treatment. Efficacy evaluation will be conducted after 4 cycles of treatment, and subsequent treatment regimens will be determined according to each patient's condition.
primary_outcomes: the complete response (CR) rate assessed at the end of Cycle 4 or Cycle 8
title: Exploratory Study of Short-Course Radiotherapy Followed by Adebrelimab Combined With Chemotherapy for Organ Preservation in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to understand how tiredness changes in adults with Primary Biliary Cholangitis (PBC) after starting elafibranor in routine clinical practice.

PBC is a rare liver disease that damages the small bile ducts in the liver.

Participants will complete questionnaires before starting elafibranor and at Months 3, 6 and 12. The questionnaires will ask about tiredness, itching, work and daily activities. Each participant will be followed for approximately 12 months.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in PBC-40 Fatigue Domain Score
Change From Baseline in PROMIS Fatigue Short Form 7a Score
title: A Study of Fatigue, Itching and Daily Activities in People With Primary Biliary Cholangitis Starting Elafibranor

brief_summary: This multicenter study will evaluate whether patient-derived tumor organoid drug sensitivity testing can help guide treatment selection for adults with refractory, unresectable, or metastatic tumors after standard treatment options have been exhausted. Fresh tumor tissue or malignant effusion will be collected when clinically obtained, and patient-derived organoids (PDOs) will be established and tested against clinically available drugs. Participants with successful organoid establishment and drug sensitivity results will receive treatment selected with reference to the test results and multidisciplinary clinical judgment. Tumor response will be assessed using RECIST version 1.1, with follow-up for progression, survival, and safety. The study plans nine tumor-specific cohorts.
primary_outcomes: Objective Response Rate (ORR)
title: Organoid Drug Sensitivity-Guided Therapy for Refractory Tumors

brief_summary:
After a kidney transplant, the amount of fluid in the body must be carefully balanced. Too much fluid can accumulate in the lungs, the tissues and the new kidney itself and may delay its recovery; too little fluid can also damage it. In current practice, doctors judge fluid status mainly by physical examination, body weight and urine output, which are imprecise and often late signs.

Two painless bedside tests can measure fluid status more accurately: bioimpedance, which estimates excess body water through skin electrodes, and ultrasound of the lungs, the large abdominal veins and the transplanted kidney. In a previous study by our group, these tests detected fluid overload that physical examination missed. Whether using their results to guide treatment actually improves the outcome of the transplant is unknown.

This trial will compare two ways of managing fluids during the first month after transplantation: one guided by these tests and a treatment algorithm, and one based on usual clinical assessment. The aim is to find out whether test-guided management improves survival, reduces the need for dialysis in the first week and leads to better kidney function at one month.
primary_outcomes: Hierarchical composite of death, graft loss, sustained dialysis and eGFR (win ratio)
title: Bioimpedance and Multiparametric Ultrasound-Guided Fluid Management After Kidney Transplantation

brief_summary: This retrospective observational study aims to describe changes in land-based motor function recorded before and after routine hydrotherapy among children with cerebral palsy. Existing clinical records from a special education and rehabilitation center in Safranbolu, Türkiye, covering September 1, 2021 through August 31, 2026, will be reviewed after the required ethics approval and institutional authorization. The study will include children younger than 18 years at the start of a documented hydrotherapy course who have comparable assessments using the Gross Motor Function Measure-66 (GMFM-66) before and after that course. No new intervention, examination, or participant contact is planned for research purposes. Changes in motor performance and their associations with age, Gross Motor Function Classification System level, baseline motor function, and recorded hydrotherapy dose will be evaluated when data permit. As this is an uncontrolled retrospective study, observed changes will not be interpreted as the causal effect of hydrotherapy alone. Approximately 45 eligible children are expected. Record abstraction is planned to begin on November 1, 2026; completion is estimated for April 30, 2027.

brief_summary:
This prospective, multi-center, randomized controlled clinical trial is designed to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of a biodegradable magnesium alloy scaffold with controlled degradation for the treatment of periarticular bone defects of the extremities. Adults with proximal humeral fractures, distal radius fractures, or tibial plateau fractures associated with bone defects and requiring surgical treatment will be enrolled. A total of 120 participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the experimental group or the control group.

Participants in the experimental group will undergo open reduction and internal fixation with implantation of a customized magnesium alloy scaffold into the bone defect. Participants in the control group will undergo conventional open reduction and internal fixation with calcium sulfate bone graft substitute used to fill the bone defect.

Participants will be followed for up to 48 weeks after surgery. The study will primarily evaluate bone healing, and will also assess joint function, wound healing, degradation of the magnesium alloy scaffold, device performance, laboratory parameters, and adverse events.
primary_outcomes: Bone Union Rate
title: Magnesium Alloy Scaffold With Controlled Degradation for Periarticular Bone Defects

brief_summary:
This study will assess the effects and safety of deutenzalutamide combined with hormone therapy before and after prostate cancer surgery, with docetaxel chemotherapy added before surgery. It is intended for men with high-risk localized or locally advanced prostate cancer who have no distant spread on imaging and are suitable for surgery.

The researchers will measure how often treatment leaves no cancer or only a very small amount of cancer in the prostate, with no cancer in the pelvic lymph nodes removed during surgery. They will also assess whether participants can undergo the planned surgery, what side effects occur, and whether the cancer returns or spreads during follow-up.

Up to 37 participants will be enrolled at several hospitals. All participants will be assigned to the same treatment plan; there is no comparison group.

The planned treatment includes:

* Deutenzalutamide taken by mouth each day, together with hormone therapy to lower testosterone levels, for 24 weeks before surgery.
* Docetaxel given through a vein once every 3 weeks for six cycles during the treatment period before surgery.
* Surgery to remove the prostate and pelvic lymph nodes, when medically appropriate.
* A further 24 weeks of deutenzalutamide and hormone therapy after recovery from surgery, without further docetaxel.

Hormone therapy will continue across the treatment periods for a total of at least 13 months. Treatment may be adjusted or stopped according to side effects and the participant's condition. Follow-up is planned for up to 5 years after all study treatment has ended.

Participants may also choose to join an optional study using a single blood sample collected before treatment and leftover tissue from their diagnostic prostate biopsy. These samples will be used to explore features that may be associated with treatment response and later outcomes. Participation in this optional component is not required to receive the study treatment.
lead_sponsor: Sun Yat-Sen Memorial Hospital of Sun Yat-Sen University
primary_outcomes: Pathological Complete Response or Minimal Residual Disease (pCR/MRD) Rate
title: Deutenzalutamide and Hormone Therapy Before and After Surgery With Docetaxel Before Surgery for High-Risk Localized or Locally Advanced Prostate Cancer

brief_summary:
This prospective observational cohort study will investigate corneal biomechanical characteristics and their relationships with corneal stromal tissue features in adult patients undergoing clinically indicated small-incision lenticule extraction (SMILE).

Participants will undergo standardized preoperative examinations, including Corvis ST assessment, refraction, axial length measurement, and corneal imaging. Corneal lenticules removed during routine SMILE surgery will be collected with informed consent and linked to clinical measurements from the corresponding eye using coded identifiers.

The primary objective is to compare preoperative stiffness parameter at first applanation (SP-A1) between patients with high myopia and those with non-high myopia. Secondary objectives are to characterize postoperative biomechanical changes and clinical outcomes during 12 months of follow-up. Exploratory analyses will investigate relationships between stromal tissue characteristics and clinical biomechanical measurements.

Surgical eligibility, surgical parameters, and postoperative care will be determined according to routine clinical practice independently of study participation. No additional corneal tissue will be removed for research.
primary_outcomes: Preoperative Stiffness Parameter at First Applanation (SP-A1)
title: Corneal Biomechanics and Stromal Tissue Characteristics in Patients Undergoing SMILE

brief_summary:
PURPOSE:

This study aims to:

* Investigate the relationship between Forward Head Posture (FHP), Pain Intensity and executive functions in patients with Cervical Radiculopathy (CR).
* Investigate whether the severity of Forward Head Posture (FHP) is correlated with the degree of executive dysfunction in this population.

BACKGROUND:

Forward head posture (FHP) is a condition characterized by anterior translation of the head, resulting in sagittal plane misalignment of the cervical spine. It has become increasingly common in the digital era due to prolonged screen use and sedentary lifestyles. Previous studies have reported that this altered posture and the associated mechanical load on the cervical spine may be correlated with deficits in executive functions, including attention, processing speed, and working memory in older adults.

Executive function refers to higher-order cognitive processes responsible for goal-directed behaviour, such as maintaining and manipulating information in short-term memory and selecting task-relevant information. The prefrontal cortex (PFC) plays a central role in regulating these functions through its extensive neuroanatomical connections with multiple cortical and subcortical brain regions, allowing it to participate in several neural networks involved in cognitive control.

Recent evidence suggests that cognitive dysfunction may arise not only from localized lesions within these networks but also from degenerative or functional alterations affecting their integrity.

HYPOTHESES:

* There will be no significant association between Forward Head Posture (FHP), Pain Intensity and executive functions in patients with Cervical Radiculopathy.
* There will be no significant correlation between the severity of Forward Head Posture and the degree of executive dysfunction in this population.

RESEARCH QUESTION:

Is there an association between Forward Head Posture (FHP), Pain intensity and executive dysfunction in patients with Cervical Radiculopathy (CR)?
primary_outcomes: Cognitive inhibition assessed by CogniFit Stroop Test
Mental flexibility assessed by CogniFit Trail Making Test (TMT)
Working memory assessed by CogniFit Digit Span Test
title: Correlation Between Forward Head Posture and Executive Functions in Cervical Radiculopathy

brief_summary: This prospective randomized control pilot study evaluates the use of intra-operative infrared thermography compared to conventional visual assessment for preventing anastomotic leaks in bowel resection surgeries. Eighty adult patients undergoing elective single bowel resection and anastomosis were randomly divided into two equal groups. In the intervention group, a portable thermal camera was used to assess real-time blood supply at the bowel margins to decide the exact line of resection. In the control group, surgeons used standard clinical judgment based on visual cues. The primary outcome measured was the incidence of anastomotic leak within thirty days after surgery. Secondary outcomes evaluated included total operative time, intra-operative blood loss, length of hospital stay, thirty-day mortality, and post-operative complications graded by the Clavien-Dindo classification system.
primary_outcomes: Anastomotic Leak

More recently, TECAR (Transfer of Energy Capacitive and Resistive) therapy has gained traction as an innovative clinical application; it operates as an endogenous thermotherapy designed to heat both superficial and deep tissues. The aim of this study is to evaluate and compare the effects of conventional physical therapy and the increasingly adopted TECAR therapy on pain, disability, quality of life, and kinesiophobia in patients with chronic neck pain.

brief_summary:
Common bile duct stones (CBDS) are a common biliary disorder, and endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) is currently the primary minimally invasive approach for their diagnosis and treatment. Complete duct clearance is generally assessed by cholangiography after stone extraction. However, conventional cholangiography may fail to detect residual stones because of air-bubble artifacts, small stone size, biliary sludge, mucosal folds, or impacted stones. Previous studies have demonstrated that occult residual stones may still be identified by direct cholangioscopy even after cholangiography indicates complete duct clearance, highlighting the limitations of conventional cholangiography. Residual stones may increase the risk of post-procedural cholangitis, recurrent biliary symptoms, recurrent CBDS, and the need for repeat ERCP.

Cholangioscopy enables direct visualization of the bile duct lumen and may facilitate the detection of small stones, stone fragments, and impacted stones that are difficult to identify by cholangiography. However, prospective evidence regarding the incremental diagnostic yield of cholangioscopy after negative ERCP cholangiography remains limited. Moreover, visual interpretation during cholangioscopy may be influenced by operator experience, and evidence regarding interobserver and intraobserver agreement remains insufficient. Therefore, this prospective study aims to evaluate the additional diagnostic value of cholangioscopy for detecting stones missed by ERCP cholangiography and to assess the reproducibility of cholangioscopic visual interpretation. The findings may provide clinical evidence for optimizing the assessment of complete bile duct clearance, standardizing the use of cholangioscopy, and reducing adverse outcomes associated with residual bile duct stones.
primary_outcomes: Presence or Absence of Occult or Residual Common Bile Duct Stones
title: Detection of Residual Bile Duct Stones by Cholangioscopy After Negative ERCP Cholangiography and Interobserver Agreement: A Self-Controlled Study

brief_summary:
Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by difficulties in verbal and non-verbal communication and social interaction, as well as repetitive and stereotyped behaviors. Home oral hygiene procedures are often resisted by children with ASD; consequently, maintaining an adequate level of oral hygiene can be challenging, leading to an increased risk of dental caries and gingivitis compared with children without ASD.

Children with ASD frequently experience difficulties attending dental appointments, as the dental setting falls outside their usual routine. Furthermore, the smells, sounds, and visual stimuli present in the dental environment may be overwhelming for a child with ASD, causing anxiety that can exacerbate stereotyped behaviors and self-injurious actions, thereby making completion of the dental examination difficult. Given the sensory processing challenges commonly experienced by children with ASD, it is essential that dental professionals are aware of these difficulties and adopt specific strategies to reduce anxiety and promote cooperation during dental visits. Despite the use of traditional behavioral techniques, such as desensitization, modeling, and the tell-show-do approach, the management of these patients remains challenging. Clown therapy, which has already demonstrated effectiveness in reducing anxiety and pain in pediatric hospital settings, represents a potentially innovative intervention in this context, although evidence regarding its use in children with special healthcare needs remains limited. The primary objective of this study is to evaluate the number of completed steps of a dental visit protocol, comparing a familiarization pathway conducted through clown therapy with a conventional familiarization pathway conducted by dental staff in patients with ASD.

The secondary objectives are to assess the level of cooperation during the familiarization sessions and to evaluate parent/caregiver satisfaction with the two proposed approaches.This study is designed as a pilot randomized controlled trial (RCT) with two parallel arms and a 1:1 allocation ratio.

A total of 46 children (23 per group) aged 6 to 14 years with a diagnosis of moderate to severe Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD Level II-III) who are uncooperative during the initial dental examination (Frankl Behavior Rating Scale score 1-2) will be recruited from the Dental Clinic of San Paolo Hospital .

Eligible participants will be male or female children aged 6-14 years with a diagnosis of ASD Level II-III, a baseline Frankl score of 1-2 indicating non-cooperative behavior, inability to complete at least two steps of the dental examination, absence of coulrophobia (fear of clowns), absence of dental emergencies requiring immediate treatment, availability of a parent or caregiver to accompany the child to the familiarization sessions, and written informed consent provided by the parent or caregiver. Exclusion criteria include a diagnosis of ASD Level I, a baseline Frankl score of 3-4 indicating cooperative behavior, completion of more than two steps of the dental examination, presence of coulrophobia, dental emergencies requiring immediate treatment, lack of parental or caregiver availability for attendance at the familiarization sessions, or absence of written informed consent.

Following acquisition of written informed consent from the parent or caregiver and assent from the child whenever appropriate, participants will be randomized into one of two study groups. The control group will undergo a conventional familiarization pathway based on standard behavioral management techniques delivered by dental staff, whereas the intervention group will undergo a familiarization pathway involving clown therapy, conducted collaboratively by dental professionals and professional clown therapists from Fondazione Dottor Sorriso.

Both groups will attend three consecutive weekly sessions (T1-T3) following a gradual and non-coercive approach. For each participant, at the end of every session, a standardized data collection form will be completed to record the number of dental examination steps successfully completed and the level of cooperation. Upon completion of the three familiarization sessions, parents or caregivers in both study groups will be asked to complete a satisfaction questionnaire to evaluate their perceptions of the intervention received.
primary_outcomes: Total number of completed steps of the the dental visit
title: Effectiveness of Clown Therapy in Facilitating Dental Visits for Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to assess how continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), a type of dialysis used in critically ill patients, affects magnesium levels in adults treated in intensive care units (ICUs). The study focuses on CRRT using citrate, a substance that prevents blood clotting in the dialysis circuit. Participants will receive CRRT with citrate as part of their routine medical care.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

How does citrate affect the amount of free (ionized) magnesium in the blood How much magnesium is removed by the dialysis circuit during treatment? How do magnesium levels in the blood change over time during treatment? How does treatment affect calcium and phosphate levels and what changes occur in the body's acid-base balance and metabolism?

Researchers will:

Measure magnesium, calcium and phosphate levels in blood and dialysis circuit fluid samples collected before and during treatment, for up to 72 hours.

Measure additional blood markers to assess changes in metabolism and acid-base balance.

Record dialysis treatment settings and fluid flow rates.

The collected measurements will be used to better understand how magnesium and other electrolytes are affected during CRRT with citrate.
interventions: Serial blood and dialysis circuit fluid sampling
primary_outcomes: Citrate-associated magnesium chelation
Magnesium flux across the extracorporeal filter
Extracorporeal magnesium mass balance
Changes in systemic total and ionized magnesium concentrations
title: Magnesium Kinetics During Citrate-Anticoagulated CRRT

brief_summary:
This study evaluates a new minimally invasive surgical technique for treating kidney stones called Triple-Zero Retrograde Intrarenal Surgery (TZ-RIRS).

Traditionally, RIRS is performed using three standard tools: X-ray guidance (fluoroscopy), a plastic tube to keep the ureter open (ureteral access sheath or UAS), and a stent placed before surgery to widen the ureter. While effective, these tools expose patients to radiation, can cause ureteral injuries, and require an extra procedure for the preoperative stent.

The "Triple-Zero" approach aims to eliminate all three: zero fluoroscopy, zero UAS, and zero preoperative stents. Because this technique is technically demanding, the researchers also developed a new tool called the "TZ-STONE score." This score uses five pre-operative factors (stone size, location, blockage, number of stones, and stone density) to predict which patients are the best candidates for this simplified surgery.

The study compares the safety and success rates of patients who underwent the Triple-Zero approach with those who had conventional RIRS. The researchers aim to see if the Triple-Zero approach achieves similar stone-free rates while reducing radiation exposure, minimizing ureteral injuries, and avoiding the need for a preoperative stent.
primary_outcomes: Complete TZ-RIRS Success
title: TZ-RIRS vs. C-RIRS for Kidney Stones

brief_summary:
Health-related social work fulfills an important function in accompanying and supporting individuals who are affected by health-related, social, and material problems. Despite many years of practical experience, however, there is still a lack of scientific evidence regarding its effectiveness, both in Switzerland and internationally. Reliable instruments for measuring the services provided by social work are lacking, as are representative studies.

The ALIMEnt II study aims to further develop procedures for evidence-based impact measurement in the field of health-related social work and to contribute to closing this research gap:

* By developing an instrument (measurement scale) to reliably assess the activities of social workers.
* By applying this instrument to examine two central functions of health-related social work: providing support (accompaniment) and facilitating access to resources.

The instrument captures which services are provided from the perspectives of both social workers and clients, as well as how clients' situations change over time from both their perspectives. This questionnaire will be used in a subsequent longitudinal study to examine the relationship between specific methods of professional practice and client outcomes.

The results are intended to demonstrate the extent to which the instrument can be reliably used to capture the services of social work, and to provide evidence of the effectiveness of accompaniment and resource provision under different practice conditions.

Investigating the assumed causal relationships under complex real-world practice conditions is challenging. To address this, the investigators use an impact model of health-related social work that was developed in a previous empirical study (ALIMEnt I). Both clients and social workers from the field of health-related social work will participate in the ALIMEnt II study.
primary_outcomes: Change of perceived stress and burden (PSS) from baseline to 3 and 6 months
Change of self-determined live conduct through the assessment of capabilities (OxCAP) from baseline to 3 and to 6 months
Change of navigation of and knowledge about the support system (self-developed items) from baseline to 3 and to 6 months
Change of self-determined live conduct through the assessment of social participation (F-SozU) from baseline to 3 and to 6 months
title: The Impact of Continuous Case Support and Resource Provision in Clinical Social Work Interventions

brief_summary:
Dementia is a major health challenge associated with population aging. As dementia progresses, patients often experience a decline in their ability to perform basic activities of daily living (BADL), such as dressing and personal hygiene, leading to increased dependence on caregivers. Apathy, characterized by reduced motivation, interest, and initiative, is a common symptom of dementia and may contribute to difficulties in initiating daily activities.

Doll therapy is a non-pharmacological intervention that involves guided interaction with dolls to promote emotional engagement, motivation, and participation in activities. Previous studies suggest that doll therapy may help alleviate apathy and improve behavioral symptoms in patients with dementia. However, its effects on the initiation of basic daily activities remain unclear.

This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of doll therapy in improving apathy and basic activities of daily living among older adults with dementia. Participants will be randomly assigned to either a doll therapy group or a usual care group. The intervention will last for 2 weeks, and outcomes will be assessed at baseline, Week 2 (end of intervention), and Week 4 (follow-up).

The primary outcome is the severity of apathy. Secondary outcomes include basic activities of daily living, quality of life, and neuropsychiatric symptoms.

The study hypothesizes that doll therapy will reduce apathy and improve the ability to initiate and perform basic daily activities in older adults with dementia compared with usual care.
primary_outcomes: Apathy Evaluation Scale-Informant Version (AES-I) Total Score
Basic Activities of Daily Living Assessment for Patients with Cognitive Impairment (C-BADL) Score
title: Effects of Doll Therapy on Apathy and Activities of Daily Living Initiation Deficits in Older Adults With Dementia

brief_summary:
This randomized, double-blind clinical trial evaluates whether adding targeted osteopathy to physiotherapy improves recovery after open surgery for Dupuytren disease.

Patients who have undergone their first open fasciectomy for Dupuytren disease will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. Both groups will receive physiotherapy. One group will additionally receive a targeted osteopathy session, while the other group will receive a sham osteopathy session.

The main objective is to evaluate recovery of extension of the metacarpophalangeal joint of the operated finger. Secondary outcomes include hand function, extension of the proximal and distal interphalangeal joints, grip strength, scar vascularization, quality of life, scar adherence, and postoperative pain.

The study will include 50 adult patients. Participants will be followed for 12 weeks, with assessments at 1, 4, 8, and 12 weeks after the start of treatment.
primary_outcomes: MCP joint extension
title: Kinesitherapy Plus Osteopathy After Surgery for Dupuytren Disease

Outcomes will be assessed using appropriate measurement instruments at the time points defined in the study protocol.
