Change in Loneliness
Change in Interpersonal Relationship Styles
title: Interpersonal Relational Role Analysis Group Therapy for Nursing Students at Risk of Internet Addiction

brief_summary: Chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) is associated with reduced mobility, frailty, impaired physical performance, and decreased quality of life in older adults. Traditional rehabilitation programs primarily focus on calf muscle function and venous symptom management, but often fail to address the heterogeneity of functional impairments observed in this population. This randomized controlled trial aims to investigate whether a performance-based phenotyping approach for individualized rehabilitation is more effective than a standardized multicomponent rehabilitation program in improving physical performance, frailty, functional capacity, and venous outcomes in older adults with CVI. Participants will be randomly assigned to either a phenotype-guided individualized rehabilitation program or a standardized rehabilitation program for 12 weeks, with outcomes assessed at baseline, post-intervention, and 24-week follow-up. The primary outcome is physical performance measured by the Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB). Secondary outcomes include frailty status, mobility, sarcopenia indicators, functional capacity, venous symptoms, and quality of life.
primary_outcomes: Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB)
title: Phenotyping Rehabilitation for Improving Frailty, Functional Capacity

brief_summary:
The goal of this quasi-experimental clinical trial is to compare the effectiveness of plasma exeresis combined with narrowband ultraviolet B (NB-UVB) phototherapy versus NB-UVB monotherapy in patients with stable non-segmental vitiligo aged 8 to 65 years.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does plasma exeresis combined with NB-UVB produce greater repigmentation than NB-UVB alone after 24 weeks?
* Is combination therapy associated with better clinical response as measured by the Vitiligo Area Scoring Index (VASI)?

Researchers will compare plasma exeresis plus NB-UVB with NB-UVB alone to determine whether the combination treatment improves repigmentation.

Participants will:

* Receive either plasma exeresis once monthly plus NB-UVB twice weekly, or NB-UVB phototherapy alone twice weekly.
* Attend follow-up visits every 4 weeks for 24 weeks.
* Have their vitiligo severity assessed using the Vitiligo Area Scoring Index (VASI) at baseline and during follow-up.
primary_outcomes: Change in Vitiligo Area Scoring Index (VASI) from Baseline to Week 24
title: Plasma Exeresis Plus NB-UVB Versus NB-UVB Alone for Stable Vitiligo

brief_summary:
Hip replacement is highly effective for severe osteoarthritis, but some patients continue to experience symptoms or complications. Robotic-assisted hip replacement uses three-dimensional planning and robotic guidance to position implants more precisely. Although its use is increasing, it remains uncertain whether this added precision improves recovery or outcomes that patients can feel.

We will conduct an internal pilot randomized trial of adults undergoing hip replacement at Juravinski Hospital. Participants will be assigned by chance to robotic-assisted or conventional surgery. The pilot will assess recruitment, delivery of assigned surgery, protocol adherence, follow-up and data quality to determine whether a larger Canadian multicentre trial is feasible. We will also collect joint awareness, function, quality of life, satisfaction, complications, operating time, length of stay and readmission. If progression criteria are met, pilot participants and data will be retained in the expanded trial. This study will build the Canadian evidence needed to evaluate robotic-assisted hip replacement responsibly.
primary_outcomes: Feasibility Outcomes
title: Total Hip Replacement: an Investigation of Robotic-assisted Versus conVentional Surgery and Patient-centred outcomEs

brief_summary: Children undergoing cardiac catheterization will be given anesthesia using either a combination of propofol and ketamine or sevoflurane gas. The time taken to fall asleep will be recorded. During the procedure, anesthesia will be maintained to keep the child asleep and comfortable. After the procedure, the time taken to remove the breathing device and the time required for recovery will be recorded. In the recovery area, children will be assessed for emergence delirium (agitation, restlessness, or confusion while waking up from anesthesia) at 0, 5, 10, 15, and 60 minutes. Children who develop significant emergence delirium will receive an appropriate dose of medication to manage the condition, provided there are no medical reasons to avoid its use.
primary_outcomes: Pediatric Anesthesia Emergence Delirium (PAED) Score
title: Propofol-Ketamine Versus Sevoflurane for Laryngeal Mask Anesthesia in Pediatric Cardiac Catheterization

brief_summary:
This study compares two common heat-based procedures for treating varicose veins in the legs: radiofrequency ablation (RFA) and microwave ablation (MWA). Both treatments use heat to close off diseased veins, but they work differently-RFA heats through direct contact, while MWA uses microwave energy that spreads heat more widely.

The main question is: Which procedure causes less pain during the surgery?

Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either RFA or MWA. Since the surgery is done under local anesthesia (not general anesthesia), patients remain awake throughout. We will measure their pain at four key moments:

When the needle is first inserted

Right after injecting the numbing fluid (tumescent anesthesia)

During the heat treatment itself

At the end of the entire procedure

We will also track how much numbing fluid is used, how long the procedure takes, and any side effects. Patients will be followed for 30 days after surgery to monitor recovery and satisfaction.

The goal is to find out whether one method is more comfortable for patients, and to identify which factors (such as age, vein size, or anxiety level) affect pain during each procedure. This will help doctors choose the best approach for each patient and improve the overall treatment experience.
primary_outcomes: Pain Score at Tumescent Anesthesia Injection Completion (VAS-T2)
Pain Score During Catheter Ablation (VAS-T3)
title: Pain During Heat Treatment for Lower Extremity Varicose Veins: Radiofrequency vs. Microwave

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if microwave ablation of benign thyroid nodules under local anaesthesia is a safe and effective procedure compared to open thyroidectomy.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Dose microwave Ablation effectively cause shrinkage of thyroid nodules? Can ablation of selective area of nodules be safely performed under ultrasound guidance, avoiding critical structures including recurrent laryngeal nerve, major vessels and trachea? Researchers will recruit subjects with symptomatic benign thyroid nodules for Microwave Ablation.

Participants will:

Undergo ultrasound guided Microwave Ablation of benign thyroid nodules. Visit the clinic at post operation 2-week, 3-month, 6-month, 12-month, 2-year and 3-year for checkups and tests.

Fill in questionnaire at each clinic visit for pain, pressure symptoms, cosmetic overall satisfaction in Visual Analog Scale.
primary_outcomes: Thyroid nodule volume reduction rate (VRR) at 3 months post operation
title: Ultrasound-guided Microwave Ablation of Benign Thyroid Nodules

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate the efficacy, satisfaction, and safety of two collagen biostimulators used to treat cellulite: poly-L-lactic acid (PLLA) and calcium hydroxyapatite (CaHA).

Cellulite is a common aesthetic condition characterized by depressions, irregularities, and nodules on the surface of the skin. The study will include 30 adult women with grade 2 or 3 cellulite affecting the buttocks or posterior thighs.

The study will use a randomized, double-blind, split-body design. Each participant will receive both treatments, with one side of the body treated with PLLA and the other side treated with CaHA. The side receiving each treatment will be determined randomly.

The severity of cellulite will be assessed using a standardized cellulite severity scale. Treatment efficacy, participant satisfaction, and safety will also be evaluated using the Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale, a Net Promoter Score (NPS), clinical assessments, and photographic documentation.

The study is intended to provide comparative information about the efficacy, satisfaction, and safety of PLLA and CaHA for the treatment of cellulite. The findings may contribute to clinical decision-making regarding the use of collagen biostimulators for this condition.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Cellulite Severity Scale Score at Day 30
title: Efficacy, Satisfaction, And Safety Of Cellulite Treatment Using Collagen Biostimulators

brief_summary: Building on promising pilot findings, this study will employ a Hybrid Type 1 Effectiveness-Implementation RCT to evaluate the effectiveness of a novel intervention for first-year college students who abstain from or use alcohol and cannabis lightly, compared to assessment-only control. Aim 1 will finalize the intervention through student feedback to ensure relevance and engagement and Aim 2 will test its impact on abstaining and light alcohol and cannabis use, related consequences, and key cognitive and behavioral outcomes in a two-arm RCT (N = 800) across the first semester and academic year. Aim 3 will assess early implementation outcomes using mixed methods, including focus groups with a Campus Advisory Board, validated survey measures, and intervention analytics, to inform future dissemination and implementation strategies.
lead_sponsor: The University of Texas at Arlington
primary_outcomes: Alcohol Initiation
Cannabis Initiation
Alcohol Consumption
Cannabis Consumption
title: A Hybrid Type 1 Randomized Controlled Trial of an Online and Text-Messaging Intervention to Prevent Alcohol and Cannabis Initiation, Escalation, and Consequences Among First-Year College Students

brief_summary: Poor graft function (PGF) is a serious complication after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) and may cause persistent low blood cell counts despite donor-cell engraftment. This single-center, open-label, Phase I pilot study will enroll three children aged 6-18 years with PGF after allogeneic HSCT who have not responded adequately to conventional hematopoietic supportive treatments. CD34-positive hematopoietic stem cells will be collected from each participant's original related transplant donor and expanded outside the body for \~10 days using the small-molecule compound HEB-001 together with the cytokines stem cell factor, thrombopoietin, and FLT3 ligand. The expanded cells will then be administered as a single intravenous infusion. The main objectives are to assess acute infusion-related adverse events during the first 30 days and to examine genetic stability through 1 year. Preliminary hematopoietic recovery will be assessed using neutrophil and platelet recovery and donor chimerism. All participants will receive the investigational cell infusion; there is no comparator group.
interventions: Ex vivo HEB-001-expanded donor-derived CD34+ hematopoietic stem cells
primary_outcomes: Participants With Treatment-Related Acute Adverse Events
Participants With Evidence of Clonal Hematopoiesis or Driver Mutations
title: Expanded Donor Stem Cells for Poor Graft Function After Stem Cell Transplantation in Children

brief_summary: In 2020, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) was the 4th leading cause of death worldwide. In France, its annual cost was estimated at 4366 euros per patient, including 25% related to management of exacerbations and 33% to hospitalization. In 2014, the prevalence of COPD in France was estimated at 7.5% of the population. Projections of the epidemiological evolution of COPD systematically predict an increase in the prevalence of moderate to very severe COPD, notably due to an increase among women and subjects aged ≥ 75 years. Management of COPD patients is multi-dimensional and multi-professional. In January 2020, the French National Authority for Health (HAS) issued recommendations for comprehensive management of COPD, including smoking cessation, influenza and pneumococcal vaccinations, therapeutic training on the use of inhalation devices, and pulmonary function tests. In 2022, the French health insurance scheme also measured quality indicators to assess the care pathway for COPD patients. Among these indicators, two concerned the care of stable patients: influenza vaccination, performed on only 52.7% of patients, and PFT or annual spirometry in 34.2% of patients. Indicators concerning post-hospitalization follow-up were also deemed insufficient, with only 41.9% of patients receiving medical follow-up within 7 days of hospitalization for COPD exacerbation, and 30.9% receiving follow-up by a pulmonologist within 60 days. Recently, in 2023, an observational study was conducted at Nîmes University Hospital, and is currently under review for publication. The study aimed to assess the profile of hospitalized COPD patients, as well as compliance with HAS recommendations. Of the 85 patients included, 59 (69.5%) had a COPD-VQ-11 score ≥ 22, reflecting poor COPD-related quality of life, and 30 (35.3%) were not followed by a pulmonologist. Twenty-five patients had not stopped smoking (32.9%), and pneumococcal vaccination coverage was only 34% (10% in patients not followed by a pulmonologist).Thanks to their daily presence and expertise in care departments, hospital clinical pharmacists can do targeted interventions tailored to individual patients. For example, during a hospital stay they can identify shortcomings in the care of certain chronic diseases and, if necessary, intervene with the patient or the care team. Clinical pharmacists can also take part in day hospitalizations (DHs) by doing pharmaceutical consultations with patients. Since 2021, a respiratory insufficiency DH has been set up at Nîmes University Hospital. This DH, coordinated by an advanced practice nurse (APN), enables multi-professional reassessment of the care of COPD patients, and targeted interventions such as PFTs or stress tests, vaccination prescriptions, help with quitting smoking and training on the use of inhalation devices. Based on these findings, and using the tools and resources available at Nîmes University Hospital, the aim is to evaluate the impact of a structured, multi-disciplinary care process for hospitalized COPD patients, focusing on changes in their quality of life, a reflection of their state of health, as well as on their care pathway. The hypothesize is that this targeted intervention will improve patients' COPD-related quality of life, and reduce mortality, exacerbations, hospitalizations, cardiovascular events, emergency room visits and consultations with general practitioners. This intervention could also improve smoking cessation and vaccination coverage. Finally, the medico-economic efficiency of this process will be assessed via a cost-utility analysis. The national supply of care for certain chronic diseases is currently limited and saturated, leading to difficulties in management and medical follow-up, and resulting in an unfavorable trend in patients' state of health. This study aims to repond to that problem, focusing on COPD, to assess the feasibility and effectiveness of a structured, multidisciplinary care concept hitherto never implemented in this region. Such an approach could make it possible to detect patients suffering from chronic diseases not only like COPD, but also heart failure or diabetes, and optimize their care through interventions and the organization of a dedicated care pathway. This care would be based on the various clinical pharmacy missions carried out during the hospital stay, and the deployment of optimized DH pathways for high-performance global care. This pilot study aims to obtain the initial indicators required to set up future comparative multicenter studies with a high level of evidence on efficacy and costs.
interventions: COPD targeted pharmaceutical interview and consultation
primary_outcomes: Impact of a targeted and multidisciplinary approach on the quality of life of COPD patients at 12-month follow-up. Control group
Impact of a targeted and multidisciplinary approach on the quality of life of COPD patients at 12-month follow-up. Experimental group
Impact of a targeted and multidisciplinary approach on the quality of life of COPD patients at 12-month follow-up. Control group
Impact of a targeted and multidisciplinary approach on the quality of life of COPD patients at 12-month follow-up. Experimental group
title: Impact of Multidisciplinary Care, Structured and Targeted on the COPD Patient's Clinical Pathway.

brief_summary: Midwives work in emotionally demanding conditions that can increase the risk of burnout and compassion fatigue. This study tests whether a 21-day online live training program, "Strategic Thinking and Shaping the Future," changes midwives' self-leadership and self-compassion. The program includes seven 3-hour live sessions, assignments, and one individual feedback session. Trained midwives are compared with wait-list midwives, who receive the training after follow-up. Questionnaires are completed before the training, right after it, and about three months after baseline. A smaller group is also interviewed about their experience.
interventions: Strategic Thinking and Shaping the Future Training
primary_outcomes: Self-leadership level (Turkish Revised Self-Leadership Questionnaire total score)
title: Strategic Thinking and Shaping the Future Training for Midwives' Self-Leadership and Self-Compassion

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether adding visual biofeedback to an effortful swallow exercise program improves tongue strength and swallowing function in adults with Parkinson's disease.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does effortful swallow exercise with visual biofeedback increase tongue strength and tongue endurance more than the same exercise without visual biofeedback?
* Does visual biofeedback lead to greater improvements in swallowing pressure, swallowing muscle activity, swallowing symptoms, and swallowing-related quality of life?

Researchers compared two groups that performed the same effortful swallow exercise program. In one group, participants saw real-time feedback on a tongue pressure device (Iowa Oral Performance Instrument, IOPI) showing when they reached their target swallowing effort. In the other group, participants did the same exercises with verbal instructions only and did not see the device display.

Participants:

* Attended supervised exercise sessions with a speech-language therapist 3 times a week for 4 weeks (12 sessions in total)
* Performed repeated hard saliva swallows in each session, with rest breaks between sets
* Completed tongue pressure tests, a surface electromyography test of the muscles under the chin, and swallowing questionnaires before the program and within one week after it ended.
interventions: Effortful swallow exercise with visual biofeedback
Effortful swallow exercise without visual biofeedback
primary_outcomes: Maximum Tongue Strength
Tongue Endurance
title: Effortful Swallow Exercise With Visual Biofeedback for Tongue Strength in Parkinson's Disease

brief_summary: This prospective, single-center, exploratory feasibility study investigates the use of diamond-based nitrogen-vacancy (NV) magnetometers for non-invasive magnetocardiography (MCG). The goal is to assess whether highly sensitive NV sensors can reliably detect and reconstruct the weak magnetic fields generated by the human heart and evaluate their potential for future cardiac diagnostics.
conditions: Technical Feasibility and Performance of the Sensor System
interventions: Contactless measurement of cardiac magnetic field.
primary_outcomes: Reconstruction of Cardiac Magnetic Field Maps
title: Magnetic Field Maps With NV Application Kit MCG

brief_summary:
The pregnant women who meet the study requirements will be included in the study. They will be randomly assigned to receive either the usual treatment or the usual treatment along with an additional medicine.

The usual treatment will include fluids given through a vein, rest while lying on the left side, and a low-dose aspirin tablet (75 mg once daily) from the 22nd to the 34th week of pregnancy. Women will also receive 1,000 ml of 5% dextrose fluid daily through a vein, from the time low amniotic fluid is diagnosed until the 36th week of pregnancy.

Some women will also receive an additional injection of a blood-thinning medicine called low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH), at a dose of 40 mg under the skin, from the 22nd to the 36th week of pregnancy.

All participants will undergo weekly ultrasound examinations to measure the fluid surrounding the baby and assess blood flow through the umbilical cord. The study will record the number of babies born before 37 weeks of pregnancy, the babies' birth weights, and the number of babies born alive.
primary_outcomes: Live birth rate
title: Effect of LMWH on Neonatal Outcomes in Isolated Oligohydramnios

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether capacitive-resistive radiofrequency, a supervised core and pelvic floor exercise programme, or both together reduce low back pain in premenopausal women with chronic non-specific low back pain and pelvic floor dysfunction. The main question it aims to answer is: do the three treatments differ in lumbar pain intensity (0-10 visual analogue scale) 1 week after the treatment ends? Researchers will also compare pain quality, low back disability, pelvic floor symptoms, urinary incontinence, pelvic floor muscle function and lumbar mobility up to 3 months after treatment.

Sixty women will be randomly assigned to one of three groups:

* Radiofrequency: nine weekly 20-minute sessions applied to the lower back and, through a vaginal electrode, to the pelvic floor.
* Exercise: a 12-week programme of supervised group sessions (three 30-minute sessions per week) for the core and pelvic floor muscles.
* Combined: both treatments at the same time. Participants will complete questionnaires and a physical examination before treatment and 1 week, 1 month and 3 months after treatment ends.
primary_outcomes: Lumbar pain intensity (Visual Analogue Scale)
title: Radiofrequency and Pelvic Floor-Core Exercise for Chronic Low Back Pain in Women With Pelvic Floor Dysfunction

brief_summary: Osteoarthritis (OA) is the most prevalent condition of the knee joint. High tibial osteotomy (HTO) is an effective treatment for medial compartmental osteoarthritis (OA) of the knee with good clinical outcomes. In particular, the two most commonly used surgical techniques of HTO are medial open wedge HTO (OWHTO) and lateral closed wedge HTO (CWHTO). However, OWHTO has been reported to have a negative effect on the patellofemoral (PF) joint postoperatively due to a decrease in patellar height and an increase in PF contact pressure, in contrast to CWHTO. Biomechanical studies indicated that the alteration in patellar height can be attributed to distalization of the tibial tuberosity following OWHTO, which leads to the patella being pulled down toward the joint lines. In CWHTO, the tibial tuberosity was reported to move proximally in a biomechanical study. Therefore, CWHTO may lead to improvement of PF joint congruity compared with descending OWHTO. Meanwhile, CWHTO has also been reported to have several disadvantages, such as loss of the large bone block below the lateral tibial plateau, increase in lateral offset due to the horizontal osteotomy, and late full weight-bearing walking. To improve these disadvantages, the hybrid closed wedge HTO (HCWHTO) technique, a kind of CWHTO, was developed. The points of difference for HCWHTO compared with conventional CWHTO are an oblique osteotomy to achieve a large contact area, a contact for the lateral cortices in the proximal and distal fragments without lateral offset for early full weight-bearing, and a removal of a smaller bone wedge to maintain leg length. Furthermore, this procedure has good effects on PF joint congruity through improvement in tibial tuberosity-trochlear groove distance and the proximalization of the tibial tuberosity when compared with OWHTO If a patient has PF-OA preoperatively, HCWHTO may be chosen to prevent progression of PF-OA postoperatively. However, HCWHTO may be performed in patients with varus deformity of the knee combined with PF-OA, because progression of PF-OA is correlated with varus knee .
interventions: Hybrid Closed Wedge High Tibial Osteotomy
primary_outcomes: Clinical improvement by KOOS Functional knee score
Clinical improvement by AKPS Functional knee score
title: Hybrid Closed Wedge High Tibial Osteotomy

brief_summary:
This study will compare two regional anesthesia techniques for pain relief after arthroscopic shoulder surgery: high thoracic erector spinae plane (ESP) block and serratus posterior superior intercostal plane (SPSIP) block. Both techniques involve injecting a local anesthetic into tissue layers in the upper back under ultrasound guidance.

The study will include 80 adults aged 18 to 75 years undergoing elective arthroscopic shoulder surgery at Bursa City Hospital. Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either an ESP block or an SPSIP block before general anesthesia. Participants and the clinician assessing postoperative outcomes will not know which block was assigned.

All participants will receive a standardized pain management regimen, including a patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) pump that delivers tramadol when they press a button. Additional pain relief will be provided when needed.

The main aim is to compare the total amount of tramadol delivered by the PCA pump during the first 24 hours after surgery. Other assessments will include pain at rest and during movement, quality of recovery at 24 hours, additional pain medication requirements, remifentanil use during surgery, and side effects or complications related to the blocks and opioid medications.
interventions: High Thoracic Erector Spinae Plane Block
Serratus Posterior Superior Intercostal Plane Block
primary_outcomes: Total PCA Tramadol Consumption During the First 24 Hours After Surgery
title: ESP Versus SPSIP Block for Pain Relief After Shoulder Arthroscopy

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to compare the efficacy and safety of aspirin versus rivaroxaban for thromboprophylaxis in newly diagnosed multiple myeloma patients receiving immunomodulatory drug (IMiD)-based therapy.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does rivaroxaban reduce the incidence of venous thromboembolism (VTE) compared with aspirin in this patient population?

What are the comparative safety profiles (particularly regarding bleeding events) of aspirin and rivaroxaban in this setting?
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Venous Thromboembolism (VTE)
title: Aspirin vs. Rivaroxaban for Thromboprophylaxis in Multiple Myeloma

brief_summary: Stroke is a major cause of long-term disability among older adults and may negatively affect self-efficacy, sleep quality, and fatigue. This study aims to evaluate the effect of a Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) program on self-efficacy, sleep quality, and fatigue in older adults after stroke. A total of 90 geriatric patients will be allocated to two groups: a study group receiving CBT in addition to usual care and a control group receiving usual care only. The CBT program will consist of seven modules delivered over eight individual sessions. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline and at one and two months after completion of the intervention using the Stroke Self-Efficacy Questionnaire, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, and Fatigue Severity Scale. The findings are expected to provide evidence regarding the potential benefits of CBT in improving recovery-related outcomes and quality of life among older adults after stroke.
primary_outcomes: Stroke Self Efficacy Questionnaire
The Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index
title: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Self-Efficacy, Sleep Quality, and Fatigue After Stroke

brief_summary:
A randomized, double-blind trial comparing low (8-10 mmHg) versus standard (14 mmHg) intraabdominal pressure during laparoscopic pelvic surgery in patients aged 60 and older. The study aims to determine if low pressure reduces the incidence of postoperative delirium and assesses changes in optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD) as a surrogate marker for intracranial pressure.

Primary Outcome Measure: Incidence of Postoperative Delirium \[Time Frame: Postoperative Day 1 and Day 2\]. Assessed using the 4 'A's Test (4AT) screening tool.

Intervention: Low-pressure pneumoperitoneum (8-10 mmHg) vs. Standard-pressure pneumoperitoneum (14 mmHg), both combined with deep neuromuscular blockade (PTC 1-2) and BIS-guided anesthesia (40-60).
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Postoperative Delirium
title: Low Pneumoperitoneum Pressure for Delirium Prevention in Elderly Laparoscopy

brief_summary: Poor sleep quality is increasingly prevalent among physically inactive young adults and is associated with adverse physical and mental health outcomes. Regular physical activity may improve sleep quality and circadian regulation, although evidence regarding recreational sports remains limited. This randomized controlled trial investigated the effects of a 4 week supervised recreational badminton program on sleep quality and salivary melatonin concentrations in physically inactive young adults. Participants were randomly assigned to either a badminton intervention group or a control group. Sleep quality and salivary melatonin levels were assessed before and after the intervention.
interventions: To be used for comparison purposes. There is no intervention.
primary_outcomes: Salivary Melatonin Measurements
title: Recreational Badminton, Sleep and Melatonin

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), immunogenicity, and efficacy of QLS2416 injection in participants with autoimmune diseases (AID).

The main questions it aims to answer are:

• What is the safety and tolerability profile of single and multiple ascending doses of QLS2416 injection?

This study consists of two parts. Participants will receive QLS2416 injection via subcutaneous administration in dose-escalation part and dose-expansion part. Safety assessments will be conducted throughout the study. Efficacy assessments will vary by disease indication.
lead_sponsor: Shanghai Qilu Pharmaceutical Research and Development Center LTD
primary_outcomes: Safety and Tolerability of QLS2416 Injection
title: A Phase 1 Study of QLS2416 Injection in Participants With Autoimmune Diseases

brief_summary: This study will examine whether personal interest in smartphone video content changes neck discomfort, posture, and pressure pain sensitivity in young adults. One hundred regular smartphone users aged 18 to 30 years will complete two 30-minute video-viewing sessions, separated by 48 to 72 hours. One session will use personally preferred, high-interest content and the other neutral, lower-interest content. The order will be randomly assigned. The same study phone, stand, seating, and viewing setup will be used in both sessions. Neck and shoulder discomfort will be recorded during viewing, neck and trunk posture will be measured from video, and pressure pain threshold will be assessed before and after viewing. Engagement, enjoyment, and emotional responses will also be measured. The main comparison is neck discomfort at minute 30 between the two content conditions.
primary_outcomes: Neck Discomfort at Minute 30
title: Content Interest, Neck Posture, and Discomfort During Smartphone Use

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized clinical trial is to find out whether Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)-based group psychotherapy can improve depression, anxiety and quality of life in adults with chronic headache compared with psychoeducation.

The main questions the study aims to answer are:

* In adults diagnosed with chronic headache, can ACT-based group psychotherapy reduce depression and anxiety symptoms and improve quality of life and daily functioning?
* In adults diagnosed with chronic headache, can ACT-based group psychotherapy improve psychological flexibility and reduce repetitive negative thinking? The study enrolled 72 adults aged 18 to 65 years who have been diagnosed with chronic headache and are receiving medication treatment for chronic headache.

Participants were randomly assigned to one of two groups: ACT-based group psychotherapy or psychoeducation.

Both interventions consist of four weekly group sessions, each lasting about 90 minutes. Study assessments are conducted before the first group session, after the fourth session and 1 month after the final session.
interventions: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy-Based Group Psychotherapy
primary_outcomes: Change in Depression and Anxiety Levels Assessed by the Depression Anxiety Stress Scales-21 (DASS-21)
Change in Headache Impact Assessed by the Headache Impact Test-6 (HIT-6)
Change in Health-Related Quality of Life Assessed by the Short Form-12 Health Survey (SF-12)
title: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy-Based Group Psychotherapy for Chronic Headache

brief_summary: The purpose of this research is to better understand the mechanisms behind allergic reactions.
primary_outcomes: Maximum Lysis by Allergic Reaction Severity
title: Maximum Lysis on Thromboelastography as a Marker of Systemic Severity in Acute Allergic Reactions

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate whether a portable laser device can accurately measure the height and length of children younger than 5 years in Quang Nam, Vietnam. Accurate height and length measurements are important for monitoring child growth and identifying children who may have wasting or stunting and need referral for health or nutrition services. Standard wooden measuring boards are reliable but can be heavy, costly, and difficult to use in community outreach settings.

The study will compare the laser device with the ShorrBoard, a standard wooden height/length board. Children aged 0-59 months whose caregivers provide consent will have their length (for younger children) or standing height (for older children) measured using both devices by trained community health workers and expert anthropometrists.

The main question is: Does the laser device produce height and length measurements that agree closely with the standard ShorrBoard and are similarly precise and reliable when used by frontline health workers?

The study hypothesis is that the laser device will show high agreement with the ShorrBoard and will be at least as precise and reliable for measuring children's height and length in a rural outreach setting. The study will also examine whether use of the two devices leads to different classifications of child wasting or stunting based on standard growth indicators.
primary_outcomes: Accuracy and equivalence of laser height/length measurements compared with the ShorrBoard
Intra-observer measurement precision (Technical Error of Measurement, TEM)
Agreement between laser device and ShorrBoard height/length measurements
Reliability and concordance of height/length measurements
title: Laser Height Measuring Device Study in Vietnam

brief_summary: The goal of this study was to find out whether REACH-FOR, a group program that helps people work toward forgiving a past offense, is useful for refugees, including people who cannot read or write well. Many refugees have experienced violence and injustice, and holding on to resentment has been linked to poorer mental health. REACH-FOR adapts the REACH Forgiveness program (Recall, Empathize, Altruistic gift, Commit, Hold on) by replacing written exercises with oral, visual, and group activities and by using examples drawn from refugees' own stories. Eighteen adult refugees living in a temporary reception center in Portugal were randomly assigned to take part in REACH-FOR straight away or to join a waiting list and take part one week later. Participants answered questionnaires about unforgiveness, forgiveness, and well-being before and after the program and one month later.
primary_outcomes: Change in Transgression-Related Interpersonal Motivations Inventory-12 (TRIM-12) Score From Baseline to Post-intervention
Change in Decisional Forgiveness Scale (DFS) Score From Baseline to Post-intervention
Change in Emotional Forgiveness Scale (EFS) Score From Baseline to Post-intervention
Change in Trait Forgivingness Scale (TFS) Score From Baseline to Post-intervention
Change in Mental Health Continuum - Short Form (MHC-SF) Score From Baseline to Post-intervention
title: REACH Forgiveness Group Intervention Adapted for Refugees (REACH-FOR)

brief_summary: This clinical study evaluated the treatment outcomes of fixed orthodontic appliances combined with anterior bite raisers in patients with skeletal Class I malocclusion and deep bite. Participants received fixed orthodontic treatment with composite anterior bite raisers bonded to the palatal surfaces of the maxillary central incisors. Clinical and cephalometric measurements were obtained before treatment and after achievement of the predefined treatment endpoints. Monocyte subsets were characterized by CD14 and CD16 expression using flow cytometry.

The study aimed to investigate whether adjunctive vitamin D3 supplementation modifies vitamin D status and monocyte-related immunological responses in pregnant women receiving treatment for pulmonary tuberculosis.

brief_summary:
The aim of the present study is to compare two types of psychotherapeutic interventions in women with endometriosis and/or adenomyosis: cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT). The study will examine whether these therapies differ in their effects on health-related quality of life. It will include women with a recent diagnosis and women who have been living with the diagnosis for a longer time.

The main questions are:

* Do CBT and ACT differ in their effects on health-related quality of life?
* Do the two therapies differ in their effects on pain-related difficulties, emotional well-being, fatigue, sexual functioning, and other aspects of daily life?

Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either CBT or ACT. Both groups will attend eight therapy sessions, held every two weeks. Participants will complete online questionnaires before treatment, after session 4, after treatment, and 3 and 6 months after treatment. The questionnaires will assess quality of life, pain, emotional well-being, and other aspects of health and daily functioning.

The study will take place at the Endometriosis Centre of Careggi University Hospital in Florence, Italy. Eligible participants must be women aged 18 or older who are receiving care at this centre and have a confirmed diagnosis of endometriosis and/or adenomyosis based on medical assessment. They must have been on stable medication treatment for at least 3 months, speak and write Italian fluently, have internet access, and be able to provide informed consent. Women with a current psychiatric diagnosis or who are currently receiving psychotherapy are not eligible to participate in the study.
primary_outcomes: EQ-5D-5L
title: Psychotherapy in Patients With Endometriosis: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Versus Acceptance and Commitment Therapy

brief_summary:
The goal of this feasibility pilot clinical trial is to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of a community-based occupational therapy protocol for people living with dementia in community settings. The protocol was developed through a systematic review of occupational therapy interventions and a modified Delphi study to establish expert consensus regarding its therapeutic components and characteristics.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is the community-based occupational therapy protocol feasible to implement for people living with dementia in community settings?
* Is the intervention acceptable to participants and their caregivers?
* Can the study procedures be successfully implemented to inform the design of future clinical trials?

Participants will:

* Receive the community-based occupational therapy intervention delivered according to the study protocol.
* Participate in study assessments throughout the intervention period.
* Provide information that will help researchers evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of the intervention and study procedures.

This study will also provide preliminary information about potential changes in occupational outcomes following participation in the intervention.

The results of this pilot study will help optimize the intervention protocol and inform the design of future clinical trials evaluating its effectiveness in people living with dementia. In addition to quantitative outcome measures, participants' and caregivers' experiences of the intervention and study procedures will be collected to further evaluate intervention acceptability and identify potential barriers, facilitators, and areas for protocol refinement.
lead_sponsor: University of Vic - Central University of Catalonia
primary_outcomes: Recruitment and retention

Acceptability
Protocol Implementation
title: Feasibility of Community Occupational Therapy for Dementia (COT-D)

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial compared three local anesthetic solutions for ultrasound-guided supraclavicular brachial plexus block in adults aged 18 to 59 years undergoing upper limb orthopedic and trauma surgery at a general hospital of the Mexican Social Security Institute (IMSS) in Aguascalientes, Mexico. Participants were randomly assigned to receive 30 mL of ropivacaine 0.375% alone, ropivacaine 0.375% plus lidocaine 1%, or ropivacaine 0.375% plus lidocaine 1% with epinephrine. The main question was whether adding lidocaine, with or without epinephrine, to ropivacaine improves postoperative analgesia. Pain intensity (0 to 10 Numeric Rating Scale) at 6 hours after surgery was the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes were pain at 0 and 12 hours, need for rescue analgesia, analgesic and opioid consumption, motor block (modified Bromage scale) and adverse events during the first 12 postoperative hours. Block onset time was also recorded.

brief_summary:
Background: Periapical inflammation is a common clinical condition, classified into periapical periodontitis, periapical granuloma, and periapical cyst. When the inflammatory mass is too large, root canal therapy alone is often insufficient to control the inflammation, and treatment typically requires a combination of surgical procedures. Studies have shown that delivering Vitapex paste through prepared root canals to the periapical inflammatory site can cause the inflammation to spontaneously subside or even resolve completely; however, there is currently limited research on this treatment approach.

Objective: This study aims to treat apical inflammation using Vitapex paste, monitor changes in apical inflammation, determine the efficacy of Vitapex paste in treating periapical periodontitis, and provide a theoretical basis for this treatment method.

Methods: This study employed a retrospective cohort design, and plans to enroll patients diagnosed with periapical inflammation and showing a distinct periapical shadow at the Department of Stomatology, Jinggangshan University Affiliated Hospital, between February 2025 and December 2027. Following conventional root canal preparation, Vitapex paste will be delivered to the site of periapical inflammation, and CBCT images will be collected at 6, 12, 18, and 24 months post-treatment to monitor changes in the volume of inflammation. Complete resolution of inflammation or a reduction in inflammation volume of more than 50% will be considered a success; a reduction of less than 50% will be considered a failure. If the success rate exceeds 80%, this will indicate that the use of Vitapex as a non-surgical treatment for controlling periapical inflammation is effective, thereby avoiding surgical intervention, minimizing patient trauma, and reducing treatment costs.
lead_sponsor: The Affiliated Hospital of Jinggangshan University
primary_outcomes: Changes in Inflammatory Volume
title: A Retrospective Cohort Study on the Non-Surgical Treatment of Periapical Inflammatory Lesions With Vitapex Paste

brief_summary:

A total of 75 adults aged 18 to 64 years with post-traumatic elbow stiffness following a fracture will be randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio to one of three groups: standard rehabilitation alone, standard rehabilitation combined with GMI, or standard rehabilitation combined with PNF. The treatment period will last 6 weeks.

The primary objective is to compare the effects of these rehabilitation approaches on upper-limb functional capacity, assessed using the Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand (DASH) score at baseline and after 6 weeks of treatment. Secondary outcomes include muscle strength, active joint range of motion, pain, kinesiophobia, and health-related quality of life.
primary_outcomes: Upper-limb functional capacity assessed by the DASH score at 6 weeks
title: Comparison of GMI, PNF, and Standard Care for Post-Traumatic Elbow Stiffness Rehabilitation in Adults

Approximately 80 patients initiating Savagen as part of routine clinical care at hospitals offering a Heart Failure Medication Therapy Adherence Clinic (HFMTAC) will be followed for 12 months. The primary outcome is the change in NT-proBNP from baseline to 12 months. Secondary outcomes include changes in LVEF, renal function (serum creatinine, eGFR), serum potassium, patient-reported health status (KCCQ) and dietary diversity (Dietary Diversity Score), a composite of cardiovascular death or first heart failure hospitalisation, and adverse events, including hypotension, hyperkalaemia, renal impairment and angioedema. The study does not aim to establish equivalence with the reference product; it will generate local real-world evidence on the effectiveness, tolerability, safety and patient-reported outcomes of generic sacubitril/valsartan in routine Malaysian HFrEF care.

brief_summary:
Parkinson´s disease and parkinsonian syndromes are associated with progressive motor and non-motor impairments that may compromise functional independence and quality of life. Sarcopenia, characterized by reduced muscle strength, muscle mass, and physical performance, is highly prevalent in these populations and may contribute to an increased risk of falls, frailty, and disability.

This prospective, parallel-group, three-arm randomized controlled trial aims to compare the effects of three levels of physiotherapy intervention on sarcopenia-related parameters and physical function in adults with Parkinson´s disease or parkinsonian syndromes.

The Education Group will receive standarized nutritional education and general physical exercise recommendations through structed educational materials, without supervised exercise training. The Progressive Resistance Training (PRT) Group will receive standarized nutritional education and participate in supervised progressive resistance trained combined with cognitive dual-task exercises. The PRT plus Instability Group will receive the same nutritional education, progressive resistance training, and cognitive dual-task training, with additional instability and postural control components. Participants in the two supervised exercise groups will complete two physiotherapy sessions per week for 12 weeks.

Assessments will be conducted at baseline (T0), immediately after the 12-week intervention (T1), and four weeks after completion of the intervention (T2). Outcomes will include clinical and functional status, muscle strength, body composition and other sarcopenia-related measures, physical performance, nutritional status, neurocognitive status, number of falls, and Parkinson's disease-related clinical characteristics.

The study will evaluate the effects of supervised progressive resistance training compared with an educational intervention and will explore whether adding instability and postural control demands to progressive resistance training provides additional effects on physical function, sarcopenia-related outcomes, and fall-related functional risk in people with Parkinson's disease and parkinsonian syndromes.

This retrospective observational study examines whether troponin levels measured before surgery are associated with acute kidney injury during the first 48 hours after surgery in patients admitted to intensive care after noncardiac surgery. Existing medical records from 224 patients who underwent emergency or elective surgery will be reviewed. Kidney injury will be assessed using changes in blood creatinine levels and the need for dialysis or other kidney replacement therapy. brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial compared gabapentin with carbamazepine for the treatment of nerve-related pain in patients with Guillain-Barré syndrome who received plasma exchange. The study tested the hypothesis that pain scores after seven days of treatment differed between the two groups.

The study was conducted at Medical Unit III, Lahore General Hospital, Lahore, and included 60 patients of either sex aged 16-65 years. Patients were randomly assigned by a lottery method to two equal groups of 30 patients each. One group received gabapentin 300 mg three times daily, while the other received carbamazepine 100 mg three times daily. Both treatments were administered after plasma exchange, and patients were followed for seven days.

Pain severity was assessed using a numeric rating scale before treatment and after seven days. Mean pain scores after treatment were compared between the groups to assess their relative effectiveness. Age, sex, duration of Guillain-Barré syndrome, smoking, alcohol use, diabetes, and hypertension were recorded, and comparisons were also performed within subgroups defined by these characteristics.
primary_outcomes: Mean neuropathic pain score

brief_summary:
People who receive hemodialysis sit for about 4 hours, three times a week, and often feel tired and weak. Exercise can help, but many patients find it hard to exercise on their own. Cycling on a stationary bike during dialysis has been shown to be safe in other hospitals, but it is not yet offered at Sunnybrook.

This study will find out if a supervised cycling program during dialysis is practical and safe at Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre (Bayview Campus). Twelve adults who have dialysis on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays will cycle on a bedside exercise bike during their dialysis sessions, three times a week for 3 months. Trained nurses and a physiotherapist will set up the bike and watch every session, including checking heart rate, blood pressure and oxygen levels. We will look at how many patients join and stay in the study, how many cycling sessions they complete, and whether any safety problems happen.

We will also look at changes in tiredness, walking ability, quality of life, and how well dialysis cleans the blood. At the end, patients and nurses will give feedback on the program.

The results will help decide if cycling can be added to regular dialysis care and will help plan a larger study.

A total of 22 adults aged 18-60 years who were medically cleared to bear full weight on the affected leg participated in the study. Participants were randomly assigned to two groups: one received virtual reality-based balance training, and the other received conventional balance exercises.

Both groups received supervised rehabilitation sessions lasting 30 minutes, three to five times per week, for six to eight weeks. The virtual reality group performed interactive weight-shifting and balance activities with visual feedback, while the conventional therapy group performed exercises such as single-leg standing, balance board activities, BOSU ball exercises, and ankle strengthening.

Balance and ankle movement were assessed before and after the intervention. The study evaluated balance using the Berg Balance Scale, dynamic postural control using the Star Excursion Balance Test, and active ankle dorsiflexion range of motion using a goniometer. The study was designed to compare the outcomes of the two rehabilitation approaches following ankle fracture.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether giving extra (supplemental) local anaesthetic injections at the start of treatment, rather than only after the standard injection fails, makes numbing of painful lower molar teeth more successful and lowers the overall cost of care in adults with symptomatic irreversible pulpitis (a severe toothache caused by an inflamed nerve) attending a public-sector dental hospital in India.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does adding an articaine buccal infiltration, alone or together with an intraligamentary injection, to the standard inferior alveolar nerve block (IANB) increase the number of patients who can have their root canal treatment started without pain and without rescue injections?
* What is the extra cost per additional successful anaesthesia of each upfront strategy compared with IANB followed by rescue injections only when needed?

Researchers will compare three groups: IANB with rescue injections only if needed (control), IANB plus upfront articaine buccal infiltration, and IANB plus upfront articaine buccal infiltration and intraligamentary injection.

Participants will:

* Receive a standard IANB, followed (depending on their group) by one or two additional injections before treatment starts
* Rate their pain during access and cleaning of the tooth on a visual analogue scale; rescue injections will be given if pain is moderate or severe
* Have the time taken and the injections used recorded by an independent observer
* Answer a short questionnaire about travel, time and earnings lost for each visit
* Receive a phone call 24 hours later about pain and any side effects

brief_summary: This is a multicentre, Phase I trial of Cytokine Induced Killer-cells (CIK\_D332) in combination with Tafasitamab and Lenalidomide in patients with Diffuse Large B-cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) who have relapsed or are refractory after at least one prior line of therapy including an anti-CD20 drug and are not candidates for high-dose chemotherapy with hematopoietic stem cell auto transplantation or CAR-T therapy. The plasticity of CIK cells allows a simple and immediate modulation of the combined therapeutic strategy through the replacement of the antibody used, without having to resort to genetic modification of the effector cells. Furthermore, thanks to the simultaneous expression of CD3 and CD16 receptors, the choice of the antibody to be used in the combination can fall on both monoclonal antibodies (bound by CD16) and bispecific antibodies (capable of binding and stimulating CD3), significantly expanding the spectrum of therapeutic options and the possibilities of combining these effector cells in anticancer therapy. To demonstrate this potential, expanded CIK cells from healthy donors were combined with obinutuzumab (anti-CD20 mAb), tafasitamab (anti-CD19 mAb), and blinatumomab (anti-CD19 bsAb) in parallel and tested against a large panel of hematologic malignancies. The combination with each of the three antibodies led to a significant increase in the intrinsic cytotoxic activity of CIKs, inducing ADCC activity against all the lines analysed. The resulting activity was comparable to, and in some cases even superior to, cytotoxicity induced by CD19-specific CAR-T cells. CIKs are able to recognize tumour cells in a MHC-independent manner through receptors typical of NK cells, in particular NKG2D, and to induce cell death by means of perforins and granzymes. In addition, thanks to the expression of the CD16 receptor, it is possible to stimulate their antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC) activity, increasing their intrinsic antitumor activity \[10\]. The end result of this approach is a lytic activity that combines the intrinsic MHC-independent cytotoxicity of CIKs with antibody-induced ADCC, resulting in enhanced antitumor efficacy. The project aims to provide a "proof of concept" in the clinic of a complementary or alternative therapeutic strategy to other anti-tumour immunotherapies, treating patients with relapsed or refractory DLBCL with chemotherapy-free immunotherapy.

brief_summary:
This non-interventional study will evaluate the efficacy of rimegepant 75 mg compared with placebo for the acute treatment of moderate or severe migraine attacks using individual participant data (IPD) from six completed randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trials. The analysis includes data from adult participants with migraine with or without aura enrolled across studies conducted in the United States, China, South Korea, Japan, and multiple European and other international locations.

Although the efficacy of rimegepant has been established in individual trials and previous pooled analyses, conventional meta-analyses provide average treatment effects based on the mix of participants enrolled in the included studies and may not reflect outcomes expected in specific patient populations. The primary objective is to estimate the average treatment effects of rimegepant 75 mg relative to placebo for moderate or severe migraine attacks with respect to pain and symptom relief in prespecified target populations, including regional populations from Europe, the United States, China, South Korea, and Japan. A secondary objective is to evaluate treatment effects within clinically relevant subgroups defined by demographic and clinical characteristics.

Because this study uses existing data from completed clinical trials, no new participant recruitment, treatment assignment, or data collection will be conducted. The findings will contribute to the evidence base for rimegepant in the acute treatment of migraine.
