title: A Study to Evaluate the Effectiveness and Safety of S-amlodipine-based Monotherapy and Combination Therapy

brief_summary:
Some people keep carrying Salmonella Typhi after they recover from typhoid fever. These carriers have no symptoms. They can still pass the bacteria into food. Food handlers in the Free Nutritious Meal Program (Makan Bergizi Gratis, MBG) cook for many school children every day. One carrier in an MBG kitchen can cause an outbreak.

Standard antibiotics often fail to clear the carrier state. The bacteria form a biofilm on gallstones. This biofilm protects them from antibiotics. Curcumin is the main active compound of turmeric. In laboratory studies, curcumin weakens the biofilm. It may also help ciprofloxacin stay longer inside the bacteria.

This study has two stages. In stage 1, the study team screens 100 MBG food handlers in Surakarta, Indonesia. Each person gives a blood sample for the Widal test. People with a high Widal titer give a rectal swab for culture. In stage 2, people with a positive Salmonella Typhi culture are randomly assigned to one of two groups. One group takes ciprofloxacin plus curcumin extract. The other group takes ciprofloxacin plus placebo. Treatment lasts 28 days.

The main question is whether curcumin added to ciprofloxacin clears Salmonella Typhi better than ciprofloxacin alone. The main outcome is a negative rectal swab culture 30 days after treatment ends.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants with negative Salmonella Typhi culture (eradication)
title: Curcumin Extract Added to Ciprofloxacin for Typhoid Carriers Among Food Handlers of the Free Nutritious Meal Program

brief_summary:
This study evaluated whether an ultrasound-guided pericapsular nerve group (PENG) block could reduce pain and morphine use during the first 24 hours after hip surgery. A PENG block involves injecting a local anesthetic near nerves that carry pain signals from the hip.

The study included 40 adults aged 20-80 years undergoing planned hip surgery under general anesthesia at Cumhuriyet University Hospital. Participants were randomly assigned to two groups of 20. Before surgery, one group received a PENG block with bupivacaine, a local anesthetic. The other group received an injection of normal saline in the same location as a placebo. Participants and the clinicians assessing postoperative outcomes did not know which injection had been given.

After surgery, both groups received morphine through a patient-controlled pump. Pain scores, morphine consumption, the need for additional pain medication, and side effects including nausea, vomiting, and constipation were assessed over 24 hours.
interventions: Ultrasound-Guided Pericapsular Nerve Group Block with Bupivacaine
Ultrasound-Guided Placebo Injection with Normal Saline
primary_outcomes: Cumulative Morphine Consumption During the First 24 Hours After Surgery
title: Ultrasound-Guided Pericapsular Nerve Group Block for Pain Control After Hip Surgery

brief_summary:
Dental implants are a routine treatment for missing teeth, but the number of implants affected by peri-implantitis, a progressive inflammatory disease of the tissues around implants, is increasing. The main radiographic sign of peri-implantitis is marginal bone loss around the implant. Early detection and correct grading of this bone loss in proportion to implant length are important for treatment planning and prognosis.

Panoramic radiographs are widely used for general screening in dental practice, but judging bone loss on them is subjective, time-consuming and depends on the clinician's experience. Multimodal large language models (vision-language models) are increasingly able to interpret images, yet their ability to evaluate peri-implant bone loss on panoramic radiographs has not been tested.

This single-center, retrospective, observational diagnostic accuracy study will evaluate how accurately five publicly available large language models (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, DeepSeek and Grok) detect and grade peri-implant marginal bone loss on anonymized, cropped panoramic radiographs of functionally loaded dental implants, compared with a reference standard established by three blinded clinicians (two periodontologists and one oral and maxillofacial radiologist). Bone loss will be graded with the Froum and Rosen (2012) classification: Score 0 (no visible bone loss), Score 1 (\<25% of implant length), Score 2 (25-50%) and Score 3 (\>50%).

Approximately 784 implant sites (392 with and 392 without marginal bone loss) from existing panoramic radiographs in the hospital archive will be included. No new radiographs will be taken, no patient will be contacted and no treatment will be given; informed consent has been waived by the ethics committee. All images will be fully anonymized before evaluation.
interventions: Multimodal large language model evaluation (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, DeepSeek, Grok)
primary_outcomes: Sensitivity and specificity of each large language model for detecting peri-implant marginal bone loss
title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Large Language Models for Peri-Implant Marginal Bone Loss on Panoramic Radiographs

brief_summary:
This study is an investigator-initiated, pragmatic, randomized controlled feasibility trial evaluating two strategies for magnesium management in adults hospitalized with acute heart failure (AHF). Participants will be randomized to either a strategy of no routine magnesium testing or intravenous (IV) supplementation, or a strategy of routine magnesium testing with IV supplementation according to standard of care.

The primary objective is to determine the feasibility of conducting a definitive, multi-centre trial by assessing recruitment, consent, intervention adherence, and completeness of follow-up over a 30-day period. We plan to recruit 260 participants across two centres over approximately 24 months.

In addition to feasibility outcomes, clinical event rates will be evaluated to inform the design of a future definitive trial. These include all-cause death, all-cause hospital readmission, and heart failure readmission within 30 days of randomization, capturing events both during the index hospitalization and after discharge. In-hospital outcomes will include arrhythmia, symptomatic hypotension, serious adverse events, intensive care unit admission, and length of stay. Health-related quality of life will be assessed using the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) at protocol-defined timepoints.

This trial is conducted within the HEART platform, a master protocol designed to evaluate multiple interventions in heart failure using a shared infrastructure.
interventions: No Routine Magnesium Testing or Supplementation
primary_outcomes: Feasibility of trial conduct
title: Routine Magnesium Testing and Supplementation in Acute Heart Failure (MAG-HF)

brief_summary:
Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is characterized by persistent distress following exposure to traumatic events and is often maintained by maladaptive trauma-related cognitions. Trauma-related attributions, such as perceiving traumatic experiences as caused by internal, stable, global, or uncontrollable factors, have been associated with greater PTSD symptom severity. However, limited research has examined how these attributions change following trauma-focused treatment in individuals with PTSD.

This study aims to investigate the relationship between trauma-related attributions and PTSD symptom severity among adult outpatient patients with chronic PTSD and to examine changes in maladaptive attributions following trauma-focused treatment. Trauma-related attributions and PTSD symptoms will be assessed before and after treatment. It is hypothesized that greater PTSD symptom severity will be associated with more maladaptive trauma-related attributions and that trauma-focused treatment will be associated with reductions in both PTSD symptoms and maladaptive attributional patterns.
primary_outcomes: Change in PTSD Symptoms as Measured by the PCL-5
title: Trauma-Related Attributions in Trauma Treatment: An Observational Study

brief_summary:
This study will compare obsessive-compulsive symptoms in adults with medial and/or lateral elbow epicondylitis (pain and tenderness on the inner and/or outer side of the elbow).

The study will include 90 participants in two groups of 45. One group will have no identifiable history of mechanical loading associated with their elbow condition. The other group will have a history of activities that place repeated strain on the elbow, such as manual work, sports, or caregiving. Group assignment will be based on medical history and clinical assessment, rather than random allocation.

Each participant will complete the Turkish self-report Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale and the 37-item Turkish Maudsley Obsessional Compulsive Inventory once, at the study visit. The main outcome will be the Yale-Brown total score. The Maudsley total score will be a secondary outcome.

The study will assess symptoms, not establish a diagnosis of obsessive-compulsive disorder. No treatment will be assigned as part of the study, and no follow-up visits are planned.
primary_outcomes: Turkish Self-Report Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale Total Score
title: Investigation of Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder in Patients With Elbow Epicondylitis

brief_summary:
This is a single-center, single-arm, open-label, Phase 2 clinical trial (the SCOPE study) evaluating the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of sacituzumab tirumotecan (SKB264) combined with toripalimab as a second-line, chemo-free treatment for patients with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic penile squamous cell carcinoma whose disease progressed on or who are intolerant to platinum-based chemotherapy.

Penile squamous cell carcinoma (PSCC) is a rare and aggressive cancer with limited treatment options once disease progression occurs after initial platinum-based chemotherapy, and standard second-line approaches leave tumors shrinking or disappearing in only 10-15% of cases. Sacituzumab tirumotecan is an antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) designed to target TROP-2, a protein expressed on the surface of nearly all penile cancer cells. By binding to TROP-2, sacituzumab tirumotecan delivers a chemotherapy payload directly to the tumor cells. Toripalimab is an immunotherapy drug (a PD-1 inhibitor) that helps the body's immune system find and attack cancer cells, and combining an ADC with a PD-1 inhibitor may work better than either drug alone. All participants in this trial will receive both study drugs via intravenous (IV) infusion on Day 1 of each 2-week cycle, toripalimab first, followed by sacituzumab tirumotecan about 30 minutes later, for as long as the treatment is helping them and the side effects are tolerable.

The main goal of this study is to determine the percentage of participants whose tumors shrink or disappear after receiving the combination (Objective Response Rate). The study will also measure how long the responses last (Duration of Response), how long participants live without their cancer getting worse (Progression-Free Survival), how long participants live overall (Overall Survival), the percentage of participants whose disease is controlled (Disease Control Rate), and the side effects of the combination.
primary_outcomes: Objective Response Rate (ORR) per RECIST 1.1
title: Sacituzumab Tirumotecan Plus Toripalimab for Advanced Penile Cancer After Platinum Chemotherapy

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial aims to investigate whether ultrasound-guided electrical dry needling with conventional physical therapy is more effective than conventional physical therapy alone in the following outcome measures: disability (Neck Disability Index and Upper Extremity Functional Index-20), average pain over the last 24 hours (Numeric Pain Rating Scale), paraspinal mechanosensitivity (pain-pressure threshold), cervical ipsilateral rotation range-of-motion, and medication intake.
primary_outcomes: Neck Disability, as Measured by the Neck Disability Index, from Baseline to Two and Four Weeks
title: Ultrasound-Guided Electrical Dry Needling for Chronic Cervical Radiculopathy: A Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the effect of isometric hand grip (IHG) training on functional capacity and autonomic function before and after sternotomy. Open heart surgery causes significant physiological stress, functional decline, and autonomic dysfunction. Patients undergoing sternotomy will be assessed for 6-minute walk test (6MWT), heart rate recovery (HRR), hemodynamic stability, rate pressure product (RPP), hand grip strength, and anxiety level. The intervention group will perform IHG training at 30% of maximal voluntary contraction, 2 minutes contraction per hand followed by 1 minute rest, for 20 minutes daily (2-3 days before surgery and 24 hours once the patient is stabilized after sternotomy), in addition to standard care sessions (breathing and mobilization exercises). This low-cost, safe intervention aims to improve early cardiac rehabilitation, reduce complications, and enhance functional recovery.
interventions: Isometric Handgrip Training using analogue hand dynamometer
Standard care including breathing and motor exercises
primary_outcomes: Six Minute Walk Test - Functional Capacity
title: IMPACT OF PRE- AND EARLY POST-OPERATIVE ISOMETRIC HANDGRIP TRAINING ON FUNCTIONAL CAPACITY AND AUTONOMIC FUNCTION AFTER STERNOTOMY

brief_summary: The study aims to enroll the small cell lung cancer(SCLC) who meet the indications for prophylactic cranial irradiation (PCI): patients with limited-stage SCLC who have achieved complete or partial remission after first-line treatment, or patients with extensive-stage SCLC whose tumors are effectively controlled after systemic therapy with no definitive evidence of brain metastases. Additional inclusion criteria are expected survival≥6 months, completion of at least 12 months of follow-up, and signed informed consent obtained before enrollment after explaining the study objectives and methods.The observation group consists of patients with extensive-stage SCLC receiving first-line chemotherapy combined with concurrent immunotherapy. After two cycles, patients with a confirmed response (CR, PR, or SD) undergo PCI. The control group consists of patients with limited-stage SCLC receiving standard concurrent chemoradiotherapy (systemic therapy plus thoracic radiotherapy). After two cycles of systemic therapy, those with a confirmed response undergo PCI.Starting from the completion of PCI, contrast-enhanced MRI of the brain (plain scan, contrast-enhanced scan, and DWI) and contrast-enhanced CT of the chest and whole abdomen are performed every three months. Treatment-related toxicity is evaluated using CTCAE v5.0. Cognitive function is assessed every three months using the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) and Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA). Venous blood samples are collected one day before radiotherapy and every three months thereafter to measure white blood cells, neutrophils, lymphocytes, platelets, hemoglobin, liver function, renal function, electrolytes, and coagulation function; stool and urine tests are also performed. The data are analyzed to determine whether whole-brain radiotherapy combined with immunotherapy exacerbates neurological impairment.
primary_outcomes: Progression-free survival (PFS)
title: Exploration of Whole-Brain Radiotherapy Combined With PD-1 Inhibitors on Brain Injury

brief_summary:
Study type: Prospective, randomized, comparative pilot clinical study.

Purpose of the study: The goal of this study is to evaluate whether adding low-dose, F-18 sodium fluoride (NaF) PET/CT-guided intralesional Lutetium-177 therapy to corticosteroid and local anaesthetic injection provides better pain relief and functional improvement than PET/CT-guided corticosteroid and local anaesthetic injection alone in patients with chronic plantar fasciitis who have not responded to conservative treatment for more than six months.

Participant population: Adults aged 18-80 years with chronic plantar fasciitis lasting more than six months, failure of conservative treatment, a baseline visual analogue scale (VAS) pain score of ≥4, and focal uptake at the plantar fascia insertion on F-18 NaF PET/CT. The study plans to recruit 40 participants, with 20 participants in each group.

Primary Outcomes:

1\. Improvement in foot-specific pain and function, assessed by the change in the Manchester-Oxford Foot Questionnaire (MOXFQ) score, and health-related quality of life, assessed by the SF-12 questionnaire, from baseline to three months.

Secondary outcomes :

1. Change in pain intensity measured by VAS (0-10).
2. Change in osteoblastic activity measured by SUVmax on F-18 NaF PET/CT,
3. Safety and tolerability at three and six months

Comparison groups:

Group A (intervention): F-18 NaF PET/CT-guided injection of Lutetium-177 (37-74 MBq; 1-2 mCi) combined with corticosteroid (30 mg) and local anaesthetic.

Group B (comparison): F-18 NaF PET/CT-guided injection of corticosteroid (30 mg) and local anaesthetic.
interventions: Patients receiving F-18 NaF PET/CT-guided Lutetium-177 - corticosteroid - local anesthetic
Patients receiving F-18 sodium fluoride PET/CT-guided corticosteroid - local anaesthetic
lead_sponsor: Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research, Chandigarh
primary_outcomes: Change in Manchester-Oxford Foot Questionnaire (MOXFQ score) and 12-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-12 questionnaire)
title: F-18 Sodium Fluoride PET/CT-Guided Pain Palliation in Chronic Plantar Fasciitis: A Comparative Study of ¹⁷⁷Lutetium-Corticosteroid-Local Anaesthetic Injection vs Corticosteroid-Local Anaesthetic Injection

brief_summary: The incidence of PED ranges from 2% to 50%, with a peak occurring 5-15 minutes after emergence from anesthesia. PED seriously endangers pediatric patient safety and impairs family experience. Early recognition can guide prophylactic interventions to reduce its incidence. This study aims to develop machine learning models with high accuracy and interpretability for personalized risk prediction, so as to improve perioperative safety and expand the application of artificial intelligence in pediatric anesthesia, thereby yielding substantial clinical and social benefits.
lead_sponsor: General Hospital of Ningxia Medical University
primary_outcomes: Pediatric emergence delirium
title: Predicting the Risk of Pediatric Emergence Delirium

brief_summary:
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a common endocrine disorder in women of reproductive age and is associated with metabolic, reproductive and mental health complications. Its prevalence has been reported to be between 5% and 15% in different studies, showcasing its significant impact on the reproductive health of Chinese women. A holistic approach to PCOS treatment that integrates physical, emotional, and mental health is lacking in China. The integration of counseling and personalized care into existing healthcare frameworks may have economic implications on patients with PCOS-induced infertility.

This study aimed to compare the effectiveness of the counselling, personalized care, and counseling-personalized care-integrated interventions versus the current module on the clinical outcomes over six months among patients of PCOS-induced infertility. The primary outcomes are menstrual cycle, hormonal parameters, metabolic parameters, and biochemical pregnancy. The secondary outcomes include anxiety and depression, sleep quality, and patient satisfaction. This study also explored the perceived challenges and barriers among patients with PCOS-induced infertility and healthcare providers involved in counseling-personalized care-integrated interventions in China.

The mixed-method sequential interpretative design was applied. The quantitative component involved a non-randomized controlled trial. A total of 192 patients were recruited by convenient sampling from reproductive medicine centers of four hospitals in Shandong Province. One hospital implemented each module. Data has been collected through a review of medical records and questionnaires. Descriptive statistical and repeated measure analysis of variance has been applied using SPSS version 28.0. The qualitative component involved the phenomenological approach of in-depth interviews of patients and healthcare providers involved in the counseling-personalized care-integrated interventions. Approximately 36 respondents were invited for online interviews via purposive sampling. A thematic analysis has been performed using Nvivo version 14.
interventions: Counselling-Integrated Standard Care for PCOS-Induced Infertility
Integrated Counselling & Personalized Care for PCOS-Induced Infertility
primary_outcomes: Biochemical pregnancy rate
Menstrual cycle regularity
Serum testosterone level
Serum estradiol level
Serum progesterone level
Serum luteinizing hormone (LH) level
Serum follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) level
Body mass index (BMI)
title: The Effectiveness of CPII for Infertility Induced by PCOS in China

brief_summary: Loss of the gum tissue between teeth can leave visible gaps called black triangles. This study will compare injectable platelet-rich fibrin (i-PRF), prepared from the participant's own blood, with i-PRF combined with microneedling. Microneedling creates small controlled punctures in the gum tissue. The aim is to assess whether combining these treatments improves the gum tissue between teeth more than i-PRF alone. Participants will receive three treatment sessions at four-week intervals and will be followed for six months. The study will measure black triangle height, periodontal health, patient satisfaction, and markers in fluid collected from around the gums.
primary_outcomes: Change in black triangle height
title: Microneedling-Assisted i-PRF for Interdental Papilla Deficiency

brief_summary:
Background: Patients with advanced lung cancer receiving systemic therapy often experience nutritional decline, systemic inflammation, and impaired quality of life. Channa striata extract and Curcumin may offer complementary nutritional and anti-inflammatory support, but clinical evidence for their combination is limited.

The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if combined Channa striata (snakehead fish) extract and curcumin supplementation works to improve nutritional status, inflammation, and quality of life in adults with advanced lung cancer receiving systemic therapy. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does Channa striata extract plus curcumin co-supplementation raise body weight in participants with advanced lung cancer?
* Does this co-supplementation lower inflammatory markers in these participants?
* Does this co-supplementation improve health-related quality of life in these participants?

Researchers will compare participants taking Channa striata extract plus curcumin to participants taking a placebo (a look-alike capsule that contains no active ingredients) to see if the co-supplementation works.

Participants will:

* Take Channa striata extract plus curcumin capsules or placebo capsules 3 times daily for 9 weeks alongside their standard systemic therapy
* Have their body weight (kg), body mass index, and mid-upper arm circumference checked (cm)
* Give blood samples to test inflammatory markers
* Answer questionnaire questions about their health-related quality of life (QLQ -C30)
primary_outcomes: Change from baseline in body weight at 9 weeks
title: Snakehead Fish Extract and Curcumin Co-Supplementation in Advanced Lung Cancer on Inflammation, Nutritional Status, and Quality of Life

brief_summary:
The aim of this study is to investigate the effect of B cell maturation antigen (BCMA, TNFRSF17) gene polymorphisms on treatment response and survival in patients with multiple myeloma.

BCMA is a member of the tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily that is expressed on late memory B cells and all plasma cells. Together with the B cell activating factor receptor (BAFF-R) and transmembrane activator and calcium modulator and cyclophilin ligand interactor (TACI), BCMA binds the ligands B cell activating factor (BAFF) and a proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL), thereby regulating the survival, maturation, and differentiation of B cells and plasma cells.

In this study, BCMA polymorphisms will be analyzed by next-generation sequencing in stored genomic DNA samples from 320 patients with multiple myeloma and 100 healthy controls. Genotype frequencies will be compared between patients and controls, and their association with response to first-line treatment, progression-free survival, and overall survival will be evaluated in patients with multiple myeloma.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of patients achieving partial response or better after first-line induction therapy, by BCMA genotype
title: BCMA Polymorphisms in Patients With Multiple Myeloma

brief_summary:
This study is open to adults aged 40 years and older who have chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) with ongoing symptoms. People can join the study if they are at risk of COPD flare-ups (also called acute exacerbations or sudden worsening of COPD symptoms) even though they use their usual inhaled or oral COPD medicines. They must have had at least 2 moderate COPD flare-ups or at least 1 severe COPD flare-up in the past year, including at least 1 while taking their current COPD treatment. People must also have a blood test result showing less than 300 eosinophils (a type of white blood cell) per microliter. The purpose of this study is to find out whether a medicine called verducatib helps people with COPD have fewer flare-ups or sudden worsening of COPD symptoms over up to about 1.5 years, compared with placebo. The study also looks at whether verducatib delays the time until the first flare-up, how well it is tolerated, improves participants' quality of life, and improves their lung function when compared with placebo.

In this study, participants are put into 2 groups randomly, which means by chance. One group takes verducatib as tablets and the other group takes placebo tablets. Placebo tablets look like verducatib tablets but do not contain any medicine. Participants take a tablet by mouth once a day for at least 1 year and up to about 1.5 years. All participants continue their regular COPD treatment during the study.

Participants are in the study for at least 1 year and up to about 1 year and 8 months. During this time, they have regular visits at the study site and monthly phone calls from the study staff to check on their COPD symptoms and any health problems. Doctors collect information about participants' health, including blood samples. They record how often participants have moderate or severe COPD flare-ups and how long it takes until the first flare-up. They also measure lung function and ask participants to fill in questionnaires about their symptoms and daily life. Participants have to daily report their symptoms and intake of certain medications in an electronic diary at home. The results are compared between the 2 groups to see whether verducatib helps reduce flare-ups and improves symptoms. The doctors also regularly check participants' health and note any unwanted effects.
primary_outcomes: Annualised rate of moderate or severe acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) (number of events per person per year)
title: The AIRWARD Study: A Study to Test Whether Verducatib Helps People With Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease

brief_summary: You will be invited to participate in a clinical study. This informed consent form provides you with some information to help you decide whether to participate in this clinical study. Please read carefully. If you have any questions, please raise them to the researcher in charge of this study. Your participation in this study is voluntary. This research has been reviewed and approved by the Medical Ethics Committee of our hospital. Research objective: peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC) is a commonly used intravenous treatment approach for cancer patients, but catheter-related thrombosis (CRT) is prone to occur after catheterization. Among them, asymptomatic venous thrombosis (referred to as asymptomatic thrombosis) is easily overlooked due to its high concealment and lack of typical clinical manifestations. If not detected and intervened in time, it may lead to serious complications. At present, there is still a lack of effective risk early warning tools specifically for asymptomatic thrombosis related to PICC in tumor patients both at home and abroad. This study aims to collect your clinical data and ultrasound image data to clarify the epidemiological characteristics of the thrombosis, identify its independent risk factors, and construct a high-precision, clinically interpretable joint early warning model, with the goal of providing clinicians with more accurate risk assessment tools and achieving early identification and stratified management of high-risk patients. Ultimately, it reduces the incidence of thrombosis and improves the prognosis of patients. Research Process: If you agree to participate in this study, we will collect your baseline clinical data, past medical history, tumor diagnosis and treatment, PICC catheterization, and complete set of routine test data. We will conduct color Doppler ultrasound examinations of your upper limb blood vessels before the day of catheterization and on the 7th, 14th, 30th, and 60th days after catheterization, record vascular blood flow parameters, and screen for asymptomatic thrombosis. We will number each participant and establish a medical record file. This study plans to recruit 1,655 people. The study period starts from the date you sign the informed consent form and the first PICC catheterization and ends at the completion of the last follow-up 60 days after catheterization. Risks and Discomforts: ① This study only uses conventional clinical ultrasound follow-up, which is radiation-free, non-invasive, will not harm your body, and there is no risk of medical harm. ② The fractional ultrasound examination, combined with data collection, will take up a little of your time and will not bring you additional examination fees. We will strictly protect all your personal information. However, in theory, there is a very small possibility of information leakage. Our hospital will adopt multiple confidentiality measures to minimize this risk to the greatest extent. Benefits: ① Color Doppler ultrasound of the upper limb before catheterization is a mandatory preoperative procedure for PICC catheterization. The cost is already included in your original surgical fee and no additional charges will be applied. At the same time, during the follow-up period after catheterization, you can enjoy four free full-cycle vascular thrombosis ultrasound screenings of the upper limb (on the 7th, 14th, 30th, and 60th days after catheterization). Multiple vascular screenings throughout the process can detect hidden asymptomatic thrombosis as early as possible, allowing for timely intervention and avoiding serious risks such as treatment interruption and pulmonary embolism caused by thrombosis. Your medical record data can assist in the clinical development of simple thrombosis risk assessment tools. In the future, patients with similar tumors undergoing catheterization can quickly predict thrombosis risks, reduce excessive color Doppler ultrasound examinations, and save time and examination costs. Privacy issue: Your relevant medical records will be kept at the hospital. Only researchers, research authorities, and ethics committees are permitted to access your medical records. Any public reports regarding the results of this study will not disclose your personal identity. We will make every effort to protect the privacy of your personal medical information within the scope permitted by law. You may choose not to participate in this study, or notify the researcher at any time to withdraw from the study. Your data will not be included in the study results, and your medical benefits and rights will not be affected as a result. As a research subject, you have the following responsibilities: to provide true information about your medical history and current physical condition; Inform the research doctor of any discomfort you experienced during this study period; Do not take restricted drugs, foods, etc. Inform the research doctor whether you have participated in other studies recent
primary_outcomes: The time when the patient developed asymptomatic PICC-related venous thrombosis
title: Construction and Multicenter External Validation of an Early Warning Model for Asymptomatic PICC-related Upper Extremity Venous Thrombosis in Cancer Patients Based on LASSO-XGBoost

brief_summary:
Burn dressing procedures can cause pain, anxiety, and fear in children. Distraction techniques may help children cope with these procedures and improve their comfort.

This randomized controlled trial will evaluate whether watching short videos before and during burn dressing reduces anxiety, pain, and fear in children aged 5 to 12 years. Eligible children scheduled for elective burn dressing will be randomly assigned to either a short-video distraction group or a control group.

Children in the short-video distraction group will watch age-appropriate short videos of their choice on a smartphone or tablet for approximately 20 minutes before the procedure, and video viewing will continue during the burn dressing procedure when feasible. Children in the control group will receive routine care without an additional video-based distraction intervention.

Anxiety, pain, and fear will be assessed at predefined time points before and during the procedure using standardized assessment tools. The primary objective is to determine whether short-video distraction reduces peri-procedural anxiety compared with routine care.
primary_outcomes: Change in Modified Yale Preoperative Anxiety Scale (mYPAS) Score
title: Effect of Short-Video Distraction During Burn Dressing on Anxiety, Pain, and Fear in Children

brief_summary: This Phase 1, dose-escalation, double-blind, multiple ascending dose (MAD) study was designed to assess the safety and tolerability of NRL-1049 compared to placebo in healthy adult participants and to determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) and to assess pharmacokinetics (PK) and dose proportionality. Additionally, changes in blood Rho-associated protein kinase (ROCK) activity levels will be explored.
primary_outcomes: Safety and tolerability: Treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs)
title: Study to Establish Safety, Tolerability and Pharmacokinetics of NRL-1049 in Healthy Adult Participants Following Multiple-Dose Administration

brief_summary:
This split-face comparative prospective study was carried out on 20 patients presenting with atrophic post-acne scars. All participants were subjected to full history taking, general and dermatological examination, photographing before, during and after the end of the treatment. On the right side, combined subcision with exosomes injection was performed, whereas subcision alone was performed on the left side. Three treatment sessions were administered at 4-week intervals, followed by monthly follow-up for 3 months.

Before the treatment sessions, patients were instructed to put topical anesthetic cream. During sessions, the treated areas were disinfected by alcohol 70%,1 ml of lidocaine Hcl 2% was administered into the treatment site at the subdermal level, subcision was done on both sides followed by 1 ml of intralesional exosome injection on the right side only. After sessions, patients were advised to put topical antibiotic twice daily for one week. In addition, patients advised to take systemic antibiotic therapy twice daily for one week.
primary_outcomes: Quartile grading scale
title: Comparative Study of The Efficacy and Safety of Subcision Combined With Injection of Exosomes Versus Subcision Alone in Treatment of Atrophic Post- Acne Scars.

brief_summary:
Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease characterized by dysbiotic subgingival biofilms, inflammation, and progressive destruction of the tooth-supporting tissues. Beyond the local periodontal lesion, periodontal inflammation may contribute to systemic inflammatory burden through the dissemination of microbial products and inflammatory mediators.

The oral cavity and intestinal tract are closely connected through continuous microbial exposure, swallowing of oral microorganisms, host immune pathways, and systemic circulation. Emerging evidence suggests that periodontal inflammation may be associated with alterations of the intestinal microbial environment and gut barrier function. However, the human evidence remains heterogeneous and does not currently establish a causal relationship between periodontitis and intestinal dysbiosis or small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO).

SIBO represents an abnormal increase and/or alteration of bacterial populations in the small intestine and may be associated with gastrointestinal symptoms and intestinal microbial imbalance. The occurrence of SIBO in patients with advanced periodontitis has not been adequately characterized. Consequently, determining how frequently SIBO is detected in a clinically well-characterized cohort of participants with Stage III periodontitis may provide useful exploratory data and may support future controlled studies.

Alterations in the intestinal microbial environment may be accompanied by changes in intestinal barrier function and increased systemic exposure to bacterial products. Zonulin has been investigated as a biomarker related to intestinal barrier regulation, while lipopolysaccharide-binding protein (LBP), or another prespecified bacterial-exposure marker depending on the finalized laboratory assay, may provide information regarding systemic exposure to bacterial products. These biomarkers should be interpreted as indirect biological indicators rather than as direct measurements of intestinal permeability.

The present study therefore approaches the oral-gut-systemic interface from an exploratory clinical perspective. It does not aim to demonstrate that periodontitis causes SIBO. Instead, it seeks to characterize the occurrence of SIBO in participants with severe periodontitis and to explore whether SIBO is accompanied by alterations in intestinal barrier-related biomarkers and systemic exposure to bacterial products. The longitudinal component will further examine whether improvement in periodontal clinical status following routine, clinically indicated periodontal therapy is accompanied by changes in SIBO status and these biological markers.

The TUN-CKDN study is a national, multicenter, prospective cohort study conducted in nephrology centers in Tunisia. It aims to describe how often malnutrition and sarcopenia (loss of muscle strength and muscle mass) occur in adults with chronic kidney disease (CKD) stages G3a to G5D, including patients not on dialysis and patients treated by hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis, and whether these conditions are linked to future health outcomes.

At inclusion, each participant will undergo a standardized nutritional and muscle assessment as part of routine care: medical history, physical activity questionnaire, clinical examination, body weight and height, body composition by bioelectrical impedance analysis (or calf circumference when impedance cannot be performed), a chair-stand test for muscle strength, a 4-meter walking speed test, routine blood tests, and a detailed dietary interview conducted by a trained dietitian. Malnutrition will be defined using the Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition (GLIM) criteria and sarcopenia using the European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People 2 (EWGSOP2) criteria. The Malnutrition-Inflammation Score (MIS) will also be calculated.

Participants available at 2 years will have the same nutritional and muscle assessment repeated. All participants will be followed at 2 and 5 years to record kidney outcomes (start of dialysis or kidney transplantation in patients not on dialysis at inclusion), major cardiovascular events, hospitalizations, and deaths.

The study does not involve any treatment or change in usual medical care. About 4,000 participants are planned.
primary_outcomes: Prevalence of GLIM-defined malnutrition
Prevalence of EWGSOP2-defined sarcopenia
title: Malnutrition and Sarcopenia in Adults With Chronic Kidney Disease in Tunisia

This exploratory case study aims to assess the feasibility and immediate responses associated with a single-session bedside Presence-Adaptive Music Therapy (PAMT) protocol in perioperative inpatients.

The PAMT protocol consists of five stages: Check In, Musical Mirroring, Awareness Facilitation, Adaptive Modulation, and Sedation \& Stabilization. The music therapist adapts the musical interaction to the patient's current emotional state and responses.

The study uses a single-group, pre-post exploratory case study design without randomization or a control group. Participants' overall emotional states will be assessed before and after the session using a 0-10 visual analog scale (VAS). Patient satisfaction, verbal feedback, nonverbal responses, and therapist observations will also be documented.

The findings are intended to provide preliminary evidence regarding the feasibility and clinical application of bedside PAMT and to inform future research.

brief_summary:
In recent years, wearable and contactless devices, including smart rings, smart bands/watches, and smart mattresses, have developed rapidly and can continuously collect multidimensional data such as heart rate, oxygen saturation, respiration, body movement, snoring, body temperature, and environmental parameters. Nevertheless, most current consumer-grade or wellness-oriented devices have not been trained and validated using large polysomnography (PSG)-synchronized reference datasets. Their accuracy, robustness, and interpretability in people with insomnia, obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), and other sleep disorders therefore require systematic evaluation.

Leveraging a multicenter clinical sleep-medicine platform, this study will synchronously collect standard full-night polysomnography (PSG) data, continuous body-temperature data, smart-ring sensor data, contactless sleep-monitoring belt data, and indoor environmental monitoring data from the same participant during the same monitoring night. A clinical sleep database will be established with PSG-derived reference-standard labels, strict temporal synchronization, and multimodal features. The database will support the development, optimization, and validation of sleep-staging and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA)-screening models and will provide a data and modeling foundation for subsequent smart sleep-monitoring products, home-based sleep-health management, and clinically assisted screening applications.

brief_summary:
The study examines how individuals with Parkinson's disease, compared to healthy older adults, evaluate their ability to cross an obstacle, and the association between this evaluation, motor and cognitive status, and self-awareness.

A total of 120 participants aged 65-85 years will be recruited: 60 with Parkinson's disease and 60 healthy adults. Following a telephone screening, eligible participants will be invited to a single session lasting 1.5 to 2 hours at the University of Haifa, a Maccabi Healthcare Services institute, or the participant's home.

During the session, following an explanation and the signing of an informed consent form, demographic and clinical data will be collected, anthropometric measurements will be taken, and questionnaires addressing walking confidence and emotional state will be completed. Furthermore, mobility will be assessed using the Timed Up and Go test, motor symptom severity will be assessed using the UPDRS-III (for individuals with Parkinson's disease only), and cognitive function will be evaluated via a computerized test. Finally, participants will perform the research task. In this task, while standing in front of the obstacle, they will be asked to estimate the maximum obstacle height they believe they can safely cross. Following this, they will be asked to actually cross it. Based on these data, the gap between perceived and actual ability will be calculated. The task will be performed under two conditions: without a backpack and with a weighted backpack (carrying approximately 10% of the participant's body weight). The performance of the research task will be video-recorded for the analysis of crossing data.

We are currently enrolling 60 adult PAH patients in a 12-week trial. Participants will be randomized into two cohorts: one receiving standard PAH therapy supplemented with a low daily dose of colchicine, and a control group receiving standard care exclusively.

brief_summary:
Moyamoya disease, also known as "smoky vein disease," is a relatively rare chronic form of cerebral artery occlusion. The exact cause of this condition is currently unknown. It is characterized by progressive blockage of the carotid arteries with the formation of an abnormal cerebral vascular network, which appears as "smoky" on cerebral angiography. In recent years, the prevalence of smoky vein disease has been increasing due to the widespread availability of various imaging techniques. Because the cause of smoky vein disease is not yet understood, there is currently no definitive and effective treatment. Management focuses primarily on addressing symptoms of ischemia and bleeding. Therefore, the current clinical approach to smoky vein disease relies heavily on surgery to restore blood flow. While surgery is believed to reduce the risk of ischemic injury, it cannot prevent stroke in either bleeding or ischemic cases.

Atypical cerebral infarction, also known as cerebral infarction syndrome, differs from typical cerebral infarction in terms of its etiology, affected areas, and clinical presentation. Unlike typical cerebral infarction, which often has an unknown cause and involves both sides of the cerebral vasculature, atypical cerebral infarction is typically caused by identifiable conditions such as atherosclerosis, autoimmune diseases (e.g., lupus), or post-stroke infection or radiation therapy. Furthermore, the vascular involvement may be limited to one side, or the angiographic findings may not fully conform to the typical presentation. In children, symptoms often include signs of cerebral ischemia (e.g., recurrent headaches, weakness), while adults may experience cerebral infarction or hemorrhage. Diagnosis relies primarily on imaging studies such as angiography.

Replenishing Five Herbs Decoction is a commonly used traditional Chinese medicine formula in clinical practice. Its key ingredients include Astragalus, Red Atractylocarpus, and Angelica sinensis. Its primary functions are to tonify Qi, promote blood circulation, and clear stagnation. It is particularly effective in treating stroke, where it demonstrates good results in cases of hemiplegia, facial asymmetry, and facial paralysis. Furthermore, Replenishing Five Herbs Decoction is also effective in treating frequent urination, urinary incontinence, and cerebrovascular diseases, including those resulting from cerebrovascular damage or coronary heart disease. Finally, it is also effective in treating muscle atrophy or paralysis caused by Qi deficiency and blood stagnation.

"Replenishing Five Herbs Decoction" has been shown to improve neurological and motor function in stroke patients, leading to better outcomes. This is likely due to the specific ingredients in the formula: ginseng, angelica root, and chuanxiong, all of which have properties that support and strengthen the body's vital energy. Additionally, the inclusion of red peony, chuanxiong, and peach kernel contributes to improved circulation and blood flow. Finally, the inclusion of Chinese yam promotes healthy circulation and overall well-being. The combination of these ingredients works synergistically to significantly improve the overall prognosis for patients with stroke."

brief_summary:
Good physical, mental and social health, particularly in childhood and early adolescence, are powerful predictors of positive life trajectories. Contrary to this, problems in these domains expose individuals to negative developmental trajectories. Schools are ideal settings to address these issues due to their incisiveness and long-term impact. However, school-based well-being interventions are not designed to be ingrained in basic pedagogical processes of school, this is, learning, teaching and studying. In this study the effects of a school-based pedagogically ingrained comprehensive well-being trial will be studied, involving curriculum embedded socio-pedagogical activities, designed to cultivate simultaneously learning and their mental, social and physical well-being.

In the Future School of Comprehensive Well-Being (SchoolWell) Comprehensive wellbeing pedagogy intervention for primary and lower secondary school students: rationale and study protocol for the SchoolWell cluster randomized controlled trial -study the investigators use a cluster randomized hybrid type 1 effectiveness-implementation design. SchoolWell involves 10 Finnish speaking Teacher Training Schools including both primary and secondary schools. Randomization occurs at the school level. The intervention is a multicomponent implementation strategy that has been co-designed by SchoolWell research team and case schools' teachers. All 5th and 8th graders (aged 11-12 years and 14-15 years), from the control and intervention schools are eligible for the study. Total of 1440 students (560 5th and 880 8th graders) will be recruited for the study (n=717 students from intervention schools and n=723 students from control schools). Data is collected from Grade 5 and 8 students representing schools randomized to experimental (n=5) and control condition (n=5). The control group in Year 1 remains on the waitlist until the start of Year 2, when the second cohort of the experiment (low support condition) for these schools begins. The purpose of the low support condition is to examine whether intervention effects can be achieved with less support than in the high support condition, where researchers are more actively involved.

Schools allocated to the intervention group deliver weekly SchoolWell activities over the full school year as part of the regular curriculum. The activities include socio-pedagogical activities, these are modes of teaching, learning and studying, promoting student mental, social and physical well-being as well as learning aligned with regular curriculum goals. Intervention schools have access to six implementation support strategies in addition to the training received as usual delivery to build knowledge and skills. Implementation and effectiveness outcomes are assessed using weekly online surveys, interviews at baseline T0 (8/2024), T1 (11/2024), T2 (4/2025) and at 19-month follow-up (T3; 4/2026) and four dialogues with teachers. Semi-structured interviews with teachers and support staff will be used to examine which implementation strategies worked for whom and under what conditions.

The primary outcome is study engagement. Secondary outcomes include measures on learning, mental, social and physical well-being. Economic and process evaluations will also be conducted to determine cost-effectiveness, program acceptability, implementation, adaptability, and sustainability in schools.

SchoolWell draws on the Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials (CONSORT) and the Standards for Reporting Implementation Studies (StaRI) in evaluating the SchoolWell intervention. Also, the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) is used to guide support strategies. The CFIR provides constructs that have been associated with effective implementation (intervention, outer settings, inner settings, individuals, implementation process). Subsequently, the Proctor's framework is followed to evaluate the implementation process. The framework stands for acceptability (treatment is agreeable or satisfactory), adoption (intention to employ an innovation or evidence-based practice), appropriateness (fit of the innovation to address a particular issue or problem), cost (cost impact of an implementation effort), feasibility (extent to which a new treatment can be successfully carried out in given setting), fidelity (extent how intervention is delivered as intended), penetration (number of providers who deliver treatment), and sustainability (extent to which a newly implemented treatment is maintained).

Hypotheses are:

H1. SchoolWell 1 intervention will have a positive effect on student-level outcomes (8- and 19-month post-tests).

H2. The multidisciplinary intervention enhances both learning and mental, physical, and social well-being.
interventions: Comprehensive well-being pedagogy intervention for primary and lower secondary school students
primary_outcomes: Study engagement
title: Future School of Comprehensive Well-Being

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the effects of Baduanjin exercise on pain, fatigue, fatigue severity, and quality of recovery in patients undergoing abdominal surgery.

A total of 60 participants will be randomly assigned to an intervention group or a control group. Before surgery, participants in the intervention group will receive instruction in Baduanjin exercises and perform the exercises once to learn the technique. After hospital discharge, they will continue the Baduanjin exercise program three days per week for six weeks. Participants in the control group will receive standard hospital care without Baduanjin exercise.

At the end of weeks 3 and 6, pain, fatigue, fatigue severity, and quality of recovery will be assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), Fatigue Scale, Fatigue Severity Scale, and Quality of Recovery-40 (QoR-40), respectively. Outcomes will be compared between the intervention and control groups.

brief_summary:
This domain will be conducted as part of ACT-GLOBAL platform trial and will have the nested domain name of IMP-ACT. Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) caused by intracranial arterial occlusion remains a major cause of disability and death. Medium vessel occlusion stroke (MeVO), involving distal medium-sized intracranial arteries, accounts for approximately 25-40% of all AIS cases. Despite best medical management, including intravenous thrombolysis, up to 40% of MeVO patients fail to regain functional independence, and mortality remains approximately 10%.

These poor outcomes prompted several randomized trials evaluating endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for MeVO stroke, including the CIHR-funded ESCAPE-MeVO trial. ESCAPE-MeVO, DISTAL, and DISCOUNT did not demonstrate overall benefit of EVT compared with best medical management, whereas ORIENTAL-MeVO reported benefit in an Asian population. These conflicting findings have resulted in uncertainty regarding optimal MeVO management and suggest that treatment benefit may depend on patient selection.

A potential explanation for the neutral EVT trials is suboptimal reperfusion. In ESCAPE-MeVO, successful reperfusion was achieved in only 75% of patients, leaving substantial room for procedural improvement. At the same time, major procedural complications were infrequent, supporting the feasibility of exploring strategies to enhance reperfusion.

Subgroup analyses from ESCAPE-MeVO suggested that treatment effect may vary according to time from symptom onset and collateral status. Patients treated early after stroke onset and those with favorable collaterals appeared to derive greater benefit from EVT than later presenters or patients with poor collateral circulation. These findings support a more targeted treatment approach in selected MeVO patients.

Intra-arterial thrombolysis (IAT) has emerged as a promising adjunct to EVT. Local delivery of thrombolytic agents may dissolve residual distal thrombi that are inaccessible or unsafe to treat mechanically and may improve both macrovascular and microvascular reperfusion. Because thrombus burden is generally smaller in MeVO stroke, adjunctive IAT may be particularly effective in this population.

However, no randomized trial has evaluated combined EVT and IAT for primary MeVO stroke. This study will address that evidence gap and determine whether adjunctive IAT can improve outcomes in carefully selected patients with MeVO stroke.

brief_summary:
This is a prospective, single-center, randomized, double-blind controlled trial. The purpose of this study is to determine whether depth-controlled anesthesia with ciprofol guided by Bispectral Index (BIS) can improve early postoperative recovery quality in elderly patients undergoing knee replacement surgery. A total of 130 eligible participants aged 60 years or older will be enrolled.

Participants will be randomly assigned to two groups using block randomization based on the Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI):

Deep-anesthesia group: general anesthesia maintained with ciprofol targeting a BIS value of 35-50.

Light-anesthesia group: general anesthesia maintained with ciprofol targeting a BIS value of 50-65.

Intraoperative BIS values will be continuously monitored, and ciprofol infusion rates will be adjusted to keep BIS within the target range in each group. Standardized pain management including peripheral nerve blocks and postoperative ultrasound-guided continuous femoral nerve block will be provided for all participants. Blood pressure will be managed following the same protocol in both groups.

The primary outcome is postoperative recovery quality assessed by the Quality of Recovery-15 (QOR-15) questionnaire on the first day after surgery. Investigators will also collect QOR-15 scores on postoperative day 2 and day 3, and record other clinical outcomes including intraoperative hemodynamic events, postoperative delirium, nausea and vomiting, pain level, sleep quality and hospital length of stay. This study aims to compare postoperative recovery between two different BIS-targeted anesthesia depths for older adults receiving joint-replacement surgery.

primary_outcomes: Postoperative Quality of Recovery-15 (QOR-15) score
title: Effects of Different Bispectral Index Target Depths on Early Postoperative Recovery Quality in Elderly Patients Undergoing Total Knee Arthroplasty

brief_summary: The high thoracic paravertebral block is a regional anesthesia technique commonly used for oncologic breast surgery. Local anesthetic is injected into the paravertebral space to provide anesthesia and pain relief. Case reports suggest that cephalad spread of local anesthetic may occasionally affect the phrenic nerve and lead to temporary hemidiaphragmatic dysfunction, but the incidence of this complication is unknown. The goal of this prospective interventional study is to evaluate the impact of high thoracic paravertebral block on diaphragmatic function in patients undergoing unilateral oncologic breast surgery. Diaphragmatic function will be assessed using ultrasound before and after the block. The study will also evaluate postoperative pain, opioid consumption, respiratory symptoms, and other postoperative outcomes.

brief_summary:
This study aims to compare the efficacy and safety of remimazolam tosylate and propofol for postoperative sedation in patients aged 65 years or older undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass. Postoperative delirium (POD) is a common complication in older patients after cardiac surgery and may adversely affect postoperative recovery and clinical outcomes. Whether remimazolam tosylate reduces the incidence of POD compared with propofol under standardized sedation and analgesia protocols remains uncertain.

This is a single-center, prospective, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled superiority trial. A total of 600 eligible patients will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive remimazolam tosylate or propofol for continuous sedation in the cardiac surgery intensive care unit (ICU). In both groups, the infusion rate will be titrated to maintain a target Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS) score of -2 to 0, with standardized analgesia and postoperative care.

The primary outcome is the incidence of POD within 7 days after surgery. Delirium will be assessed using the Confusion Assessment Method for the ICU (CAM-ICU) in patients who are intubated or unable to communicate verbally, and the Chinese version of the 3-Minute Diagnostic Interview for Confusion Assessment Method (3D-CAM-CN) in patients who are able to communicate.

Secondary clinical outcomes include time to first delirium, delirium duration and severity, achievement of the target sedation level, pain scores, rescue sedative use, time to extubation, ICU length of stay, hospital length of stay, and safety outcomes, including hypotension, bradycardia, and vasopressor use.

This study aims to determine whether remimazolam tosylate reduces the incidence of POD compared with propofol in older patients after cardiac surgery. The findings may provide clinical evidence to guide postoperative sedative selection and help improve delirium prevention and postoperative recovery in this population.
lead_sponsor: Nanjing First Hospital, Nanjing Medical University
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Postoperative Delirium Within 7 Days After Surgery
title: The Effect of Remimazolam Tosylate on the Incidence of Postoperative Delirium in Older Patients Undergoing Cardiac Surgery: A Prospective Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
This study will compare therapeutic holding with traditional restraint during blood-draw venipuncture in children aged 3 to 6 years. The study will include 64 children who require venous blood sampling for routine diagnostic testing.

Children will be assigned to one of two groups using a predetermined non-random allocation method. In the therapeutic holding group, the child will sit upright on a parent's or caregiver's lap in a chest-to-chest straddle position. The caregiver will hold the child securely and comfortably while the arm used for venipuncture is safely stabilized. In the traditional restraint group, the child will lie on their back and receive the usual physical stabilization used during venipuncture by a parent, nurse, or assistant.

The study will assess children's behavioral distress, pulse rate, respiratory rate, and oxygen saturation before, during, and after venipuncture. It will also record whether blood collection is successful on the first needle insertion and the total number of attempts needed.

The purpose of the study is to determine whether therapeutic holding is associated with lower behavioral distress, greater stability of vital signs, and a higher rate of successful first-stick venipuncture compared with traditional restraint.

brief_summary:
Background \& Rationale: Intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH) is a recognized hallmark and critical driver of therapeutic resistance, rapid disease progression, and poor survival across solid malignancies, notably advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). While tissue biopsies provide histopathologic confirmation, they are invasive and subject to severe spatial sampling bias. Standard whole-tumor radiomics from single-modality CT often masks localized subregional ecological niches. 18F-FDG PET/CT unites glucose metabolic activity with anatomical resolution, offering an ideal non-invasive tool to map whole-tumor spatial and functional heterogeneity in vivo.

Methods \& Design: In this multicenter, bidirectional (retrospective and prospective) observational cohort study, 900 advanced NSCLC patients receiving first-line systemic therapies (chemotherapy, anti-PD-1 immunotherapy, and EGFR-TKIs) were enrolled. Baseline 18F-FDG PET/CT scans obtained within 2 weeks prior to therapy were partitioned into distinct biological habitats using entropy-intensity clustering. IBSI-compliant radiomic features were extracted to develop treatment-specific imaging intratumoral heterogeneity (IITH) signatures. Diagnostic accuracy for staging/metastases and prognostic performance for 6-month progression status, progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS) were comprehensively validated across internal, external multicenter, and independent prospective cohorts, with biological explainability benchmarked against digital histopathology (HoVer-Net nuclear morphometrics) and transcriptomics.
interventions: This is an observational study with no intervention.
primary_outcomes: 6-Month Progression-Free Survival [PFS] Status
title: PET/CT-Based Intratumoral Heterogeneity and Multimodal Imaging for Tumor Diagnosis and Prognosis
